cards.cue: Your friend has dreamed of writing a novel for years but has never written a page. You tell her to write the first paragraph tonight.

ctx.s: 想学好英语，就从今天背十个单词开始吧，{千里之行，始于足下}。
ctx.en: If you want to get good at English, start by learning ten words today. Every long journey begins with one step.

ctx.s: 别总说要锻炼身体了，{千里之行，始于足下}，今晚先去散散步。
ctx.en: Stop just saying you'll get fit. Every journey starts with a first step: go for a walk tonight.

ctx.s: “这么大的项目，从哪儿做起啊？”“{千里之行，始于足下}，先把计划书写出来。”
ctx.en: "A project this big, where do we even start?" "Every journey begins with a single step. Write the proposal first."

ctx.s: 他的公司如今很有名，可{千里之行，始于足下}，当年他是在车库里起步的。
ctx.en: His company is famous now, but every great journey starts with a first step: back then he began in a garage.

ctx.s: 校长在开学典礼上说：“{千里之行，始于足下}，希望同学们从每一天的小事做起。”
ctx.en: At the opening ceremony the principal said: "A journey of a thousand miles begins with one step. I hope you will all start with the small things of each day."

ctx.s: 改革的目标很远大，但{千里之行，始于足下}，必须先解决眼前最具体的问题。
ctx.en: The goals of the reform are ambitious, but every journey begins with a single step: the most concrete problems at hand must be solved first.

bad.s: 我每天走路上班，真是{千里之行，始于足下}。
bad.en: (meant: I walk to work every day)
bad.why: It is about making a first step towards a big goal, not about literally travelling on foot.

bad.s: 他的论文马上就写完了，{千里之行，始于足下}。
bad.en: (meant: his thesis is almost finished)
bad.why: It urges a beginning, so it belongs at the start of a long task, not when the task is nearly done.

cards.r: shī bài shì chéng gōng zhī mǔ
cards.mean: failures pave the way to eventual success
cards.lit: failure is the mother of success: success is born out of failure

use.how: A complete sentence, said to comfort or encourage someone after a failure, or to explain why one keeps trying: 别灰心，失败是成功之母。

near.diff: 吃一堑，长一智 stresses the lesson a setback teaches; 失败是成功之母 stresses that failures lead on to success in the end.

cards.cue: A friend's first business has just collapsed and he wants to give up for good. You remind him that most successful people failed many times first.

ctx.s: 这次没考好没关系，{失败是成功之母}，下次一定能成功。
ctx.en: It doesn't matter that the exam went badly this time. Failure is the mother of success: next time you'll make it.

ctx.s: 爸爸拍拍我的肩膀说：“别灰心，{失败是成功之母}嘛。”
ctx.en: Dad patted me on the shoulder and said: "Don't lose heart. Failure leads to success, you know."

ctx.s: 实验做了几十次都不成功，可他相信{失败是成功之母}，一直没放弃。
ctx.en: The experiment failed dozens of times, but he believed failure paves the way to success and never gave up.

ctx.s: 你不是常说{失败是成功之母}吗？怎么输了一场比赛就不想练了？
ctx.en: Aren't you always saying failure is the mother of success? So why do you want to quit training after losing one match?

ctx.s: {失败是成功之母}，但前提是你得认真总结每一次失败的原因。
ctx.en: Failure leads to success, but only if you work out properly why you failed each time.

ctx.s: 这本书告诉读者，{失败是成功之母}，成功的企业家大多失败过很多次。
ctx.en: The book tells its readers that failure is the mother of success: most successful entrepreneurs have failed many times.

bad.s: 他做什么都成功，从来没失败过，真是{失败是成功之母}。
bad.en: (meant: he succeeds at everything and has never failed)
bad.why: It says failures lead to success, so it cannot describe someone who has never failed.

bad.s: 他赢了几场就骄傲了，结果输得很惨，这就是{失败是成功之母}。
bad.en: (meant: his success made him arrogant and caused his defeat)
bad.why: It says failure gives birth to success, not that success breeds failure; the direction is reversed.

cards.r: bù pà màn, jiù pà zhàn
cards.mean: slow progress is fine; the only real danger is stopping
cards.lit: don't fear going slowly, only fear standing still

use.how: Quoted as encouragement to someone whose progress is slow: keep going at any pace, just don't stop. 学语言不怕慢，就怕站。

near.diff: 三天打鱼，两天晒网 criticises on-and-off effort; 不怕慢，就怕站 encourages steady effort, however slow.
一口吃不成胖子 warns against expecting fast results; 不怕慢，就怕站 warns against stopping altogether.

cards.cue: A classmate complains she only gets through one page of her textbook a day while others do five. You tell her the pace doesn't matter as long as she never stops.

ctx.s: 每天跑一点点也好，{不怕慢，就怕站}。
ctx.en: Even running just a little each day is good. Slow is fine; stopping is the problem.

ctx.s: 我练钢琴进步很慢，老师说：“{不怕慢，就怕站}，坚持下去就行。”
ctx.en: I was making slow progress on the piano, and my teacher said: "Slow is fine, just don't stop. Keep at it."

ctx.s: “我一天只能看两页书，是不是太慢了？”“{不怕慢，就怕站}，别停就好。”
ctx.en: "I can only read two pages a day. Is that too slow?" "Slow doesn't matter, stopping does. Just don't stop."

ctx.s: 爷爷学用智能手机学了半年，他常说{不怕慢，就怕站}。
ctx.en: Grandpa spent half a year learning to use a smartphone. He often says going slowly is fine as long as you don't stop.

ctx.s: 康复训练很辛苦，医生鼓励他：{不怕慢，就怕站}，每天都要动一动。
ctx.en: Rehab was hard, and the doctor encouraged him: slow is fine, just don't stop; move a little every day.

ctx.s: 做研究{不怕慢，就怕站}，哪怕每周只前进一小步，积累起来也很可观。
ctx.en: In research, slowness is no danger, stopping is: even one small step a week adds up to a lot.

bad.s: 公交车开得太慢了，还老停车，真是{不怕慢，就怕站}。
bad.en: (meant: the bus is slow and keeps stopping)
bad.why: It is about keeping up one's own effort, not about vehicles or traffic.

bad.s: 这个工作很急，大家{不怕慢，就怕站}，明天必须做完。
bad.en: (meant: this job is urgent and must be done by tomorrow)
bad.why: It accepts slow progress, so it cannot be used to press people for speed before a deadline.

cards.t: 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针
cards.r: zhǐ yào gōng fu shēn, tiě chǔ mó chéng zhēn
cards.mean: keep grinding away patiently and even the hardest job gets done
cards.lit: put in enough effort and even an iron pestle can be ground down into a needle

story.text: A traditional tale about the poet Li Bai. As a boy he grew tired of his studies and left them. By a stream he met an old woman rubbing an iron pestle on a stone. When he asked what she was doing, she said she was grinding it into a needle. Struck by her persistence, he went back and finished his studies. The stream came to be called Grinding Needle Stream.
story.source: 宋·祝穆《方舆胜览》磨针溪条

use.how: Quoted whole to encourage someone facing a long, hard task, or to explain a success won by years of patient work: 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针，你一定能学会。

near.t: 世上无难事，只怕有心人
near.diff: 世上无难事，只怕有心人 stresses determination; 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针 stresses long, patient labour over time.

cards.cue: Your nephew wants to give up the erhu after one month. You tell him that years of slow, patient practice will wear down any difficulty in the end.

ctx.s: 毛笔字难写也别怕，{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
ctx.en: Don't be put off because calligraphy is hard. Keep at it long enough and anything can be done.

ctx.s: 妈妈对我说：“每天练一小时，{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。”
ctx.en: Mum said to me: "Practise an hour every day. With enough patient work, you'll get there."

ctx.s: 他从一句汉语都不会，每天苦学，坚持了五年，终于当上了翻译，真是{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
ctx.en: He didn't know a word of Chinese, studied hard every day for five years and finally became an interpreter: patient effort really can do anything.

ctx.s: “这么难的曲子，我真能弹下来吗？”“{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}，慢慢练。”
ctx.en: "Can I really learn to play such a hard piece?" "Put in the work and you can grind an iron bar into a needle. Practise bit by bit."

ctx.s: 老木匠花了十年才练成这手艺，他说这就叫{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
ctx.en: The old carpenter took ten years to master his craft. That, he said, is what patient work can do.

ctx.s: 写论文的那两年，我常拿{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}这句话给自己打气。
ctx.en: In the two years I spent on my thesis, I often cheered myself up with the saying that patience can grind iron into a needle.

bad.s: 这份报告明天就要交，{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}，今晚赶完吧。
bad.en: (meant: the report is due tomorrow, let's rush it out tonight)
bad.why: It is about long, patient effort over time, not a quick push the night before a deadline.

bad.s: 他天生聪明，什么一学就会，真是{只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针}。
bad.en: (meant: he is naturally gifted and picks everything up at once)
bad.why: It credits years of persistence, not talent or learning things quickly.

cards.r: yī fēn gēng yún, yī fēn shōu huò
cards.mean: what you gain matches the hard work you put in
cards.lit: one share of ploughing and weeding brings one share of harvest

use.how: Quoted as a full sentence about effort and reward matching, to encourage hard work or explain someone's well-earned results: 一分耕耘，一分收获，这是你努力的结果。

near.diff: 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆 says results match the kind of deed, good or bad; 一分耕耘，一分收获 says reward matches the amount of honest effort.

cards.cue: The student who put in the most hours of revision all term gets the top score, and the teacher points out to the class why.

ctx.s: 他每天早起练习，终于拿了冠军，{一分耕耘，一分收获}。
ctx.en: He got up early to train every day and finally won the championship. You reap what your hard work earns.

ctx.s: 别羡慕别人的成绩，{一分耕耘，一分收获}，人家比你努力多了。
ctx.en: Don't envy other people's grades. What you get matches what you put in, and they worked much harder than you.

ctx.s: 老师在成绩单上写道：{一分耕耘，一分收获}，继续加油！
ctx.en: The teacher wrote on the report card: your results reflect your hard work. Keep it up!

ctx.s: “你的店生意怎么这么好？”“{一分耕耘，一分收获}，我们每天干到半夜。”
ctx.en: "How is your shop doing so well?" "You get out what you put in. We work until midnight every day."

ctx.s: 这本词典编了整整八年，{一分耕耘，一分收获}，出版后大受欢迎。
ctx.en: The dictionary took eight full years to compile, and the effort paid off: it was a great success when it came out.

ctx.s: 考前偷懒的人别指望奇迹，{一分耕耘，一分收获}的道理谁都懂。
ctx.en: People who slack off before an exam shouldn't hope for a miracle; everyone knows that reward matches effort.

bad.s: 他偷了别人的钱，被抓了，真是{一分耕耘，一分收获}。
bad.en: (meant: he stole money and got caught, it served him right)
bad.why: It is about honest work earning its reward, not about wrongdoing being punished.

bad.s: 我买彩票中了大奖，{一分耕耘，一分收获}！
bad.en: (meant: I won the lottery!)
bad.why: It credits hard work for the reward; a lottery win is pure luck, so the saying does not fit.

cards.r: zhòng guā dé guā, zhòng dòu dé dòu
cards.mean: you reap what you sow: deeds bring their matching consequences
cards.lit: plant melons and you get melons, plant beans and you get beans

use.how: Quoted whole to say that what someone gets is the natural result of what they did, good or bad; often a warning or a comment on deserved results.

near.diff: 一分耕耘，一分收获 links the size of the reward to the amount of effort; 种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆 links the kind of result to the kind of deed.

cards.cue: A man who never visited his own parents complains that his grown children never call him. His sister says he taught them by example.

ctx.s: {种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，你平时对人好，别人也会对你好。
ctx.en: You reap what you sow: if you treat people well, they'll treat you well too.

ctx.s: 他年轻时从不照顾父母，现在儿女也不管他，真是{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
ctx.en: When he was young he never looked after his parents, and now his children don't look after him. He's reaping what he sowed.

ctx.s: “为什么大家都不愿意跟他合作？”“{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，他以前骗过太多人了。”
ctx.en: "Why does nobody want to work with him?" "You reap what you sow. He's cheated too many people."

ctx.s: 奶奶常说{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，做什么样的事，就有什么样的结果。
ctx.en: Grandma often says you reap what you sow: whatever you do brings the result that matches it.

ctx.s: 公司只顾赚钱不顾质量，最后丢了客户，这叫{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
ctx.en: The company cared only about profit and not quality, and in the end it lost its customers. That's reaping what you sow.

ctx.s: 教育孩子也是{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}，从小惯着他，长大了就别怪他不懂事。
ctx.en: Raising children is the same: you reap what you sow. Spoil a child when he's small and you can't complain when he grows up thoughtless.

bad.s: 他工作很努力，可还是没升职，{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
bad.en: (meant: he worked hard but still wasn't promoted, which is unfair)
bad.why: It says results match deeds, so it cannot describe a case where hard work went unrewarded.

bad.s: 我们俩一个爱吃甜，一个爱吃辣，真是{种瓜得瓜，种豆得豆}。
bad.en: (meant: one of us likes sweet food and the other spicy, we have different tastes)
bad.why: It is about deeds and their consequences, not about people being different from each other.

cards.r: bǎi wén bù rú yī jiàn
cards.mean: seeing for yourself beats hearing about it a hundred times
cards.lit: hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once

story.text: In the Western Han, when the Qiang peoples rose up on the northwest frontier, Emperor Xuan asked the veteran general Zhao Chongguo, then over seventy, what strategy to follow and how many troops he would need. Zhao replied that hearing about it a hundred times was not as good as seeing it once: a campaign could not be planned from afar, so he would ride to the frontier himself and then present his plan.

use.how: Said on seeing a place or thing in person after hearing about it, often as 真是百闻不如一见; also used to urge someone to go and look for themselves.

near.diff: 读万卷书，行万里路 recommends both reading and travel as a way of learning; 百闻不如一见 says one direct look beats any amount of hearsay.

cards.cue: You had read dozens of articles about the Great Wall, but standing on it for the first time you realise none of them came close to the real thing.

ctx.s: 早就听说这里风景美，今天来了才知道，真是{百闻不如一见}。
ctx.en: I'd long heard the scenery here was beautiful, but only now that I'm here do I get it. Seeing really is believing.

ctx.s: “那家店真有那么好吃吗？”“{百闻不如一见}，周末带你去尝尝。”
ctx.en: "Is that place really that good?" "Better to find out for yourself. I'll take you there this weekend."

ctx.s: 客户听了半天介绍还是不放心，经理说：“{百闻不如一见}，请您来工厂看看吧。”
ctx.en: After a long presentation the client was still unsure, so the manager said: "Seeing beats hearing. Please come and look at the factory."

ctx.s: 照片上的大熊猫已经很可爱了，可{百闻不如一见}，真的熊猫更招人喜欢。
ctx.en: Pandas look cute enough in photos, but seeing one is something else: the real thing is even more adorable.

ctx.s: 他在书上读过很多次沙漠，可{百闻不如一见}，站在沙丘上那一刻他说不出话来。
ctx.en: He had read about the desert many times, but seeing it was different: standing on the dunes, he was lost for words.

ctx.s: {百闻不如一见}，调查组决定亲自到现场了解情况，而不是只听汇报。
ctx.en: Seeing for themselves beats any report, so the investigators decided to go to the site in person rather than just listen to briefings.

bad.s: 这首歌我听了一百遍，{百闻不如一见}，越听越喜欢。
bad.en: (meant: I've listened to this song a hundred times and like it more each time)
bad.why: It says seeing something in person beats hearing about it, not anything about listening to music again and again.

bad.s: 照片可能是假的，{百闻不如一见}，别相信你看到的。
bad.en: (meant: photos may be fake, don't trust what you see)
bad.why: It says the opposite: trust what you see with your own eyes over what you are told.

cards.t: 好事不出门，坏事传千里
cards.r: hǎo shì bù chū mén, huài shì chuán qiān lǐ
cards.mean: bad news travels fast while good deeds go unheard of
cards.lit: good deeds never get out of the door, bad deeds travel a thousand li

use.how: Quoted as a rueful comment that a mistake or scandal spreads fast and far while good things go unnoticed; also a warning to watch one's behaviour.

near.diff: 纸包不住火 says a hidden truth will come out in the end; 好事不出门，坏事传千里 says bad news spreads fast while good news does not.

cards.cue: Your neighbour volunteered at the animal shelter for years without anyone noticing, but the one time he shouted at a delivery driver, the whole street was talking about it by evening.

ctx.s: 我昨天就迟到了一次，今天全公司都知道了，真是{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
ctx.en: I was late just once yesterday and today the whole company knows. Bad news really does travel fast.

ctx.s: {好事不出门，坏事传千里}，你在外面一定要注意自己的言行。
ctx.en: Good deeds go unnoticed but bad ones spread everywhere, so mind how you behave when you're out.

ctx.s: “我才说错一句话，怎么连隔壁部门都知道了？”“{好事不出门，坏事传千里}嘛。”
ctx.en: "I said one wrong thing, so how come even the department next door knows?" "Bad news travels fast, doesn't it."

ctx.s: 那家餐厅出了一次食品安全问题就上了热搜，{好事不出门，坏事传千里}啊。
ctx.en: That restaurant had one food safety problem and it was instantly trending online. Bad news really does spread.

ctx.s: 他默默帮了邻居很多年没人提，吵一次架却人人皆知，这就是{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
ctx.en: He quietly helped his neighbours for years and nobody mentioned it, yet one quarrel and everyone knew. Good deeds go unheard of, bad news travels far.

ctx.s: 网络时代，{好事不出门，坏事传千里}的现象更加明显，一条差评一夜就能传遍全网。
ctx.en: In the internet age, the way bad news outruns good is even more obvious: one bad review can spread across the whole web overnight.

bad.s: 他中奖的好消息很快传遍了全村，真是{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
bad.en: (meant: the good news of his win spread through the whole village)
bad.why: It says good news stays unknown; it cannot describe good news spreading.

bad.s: 外面太危险了，你别出门，{好事不出门，坏事传千里}。
bad.en: (meant: it's dangerous out there, stay at home)
bad.why: It is about how gossip and bad news spread, not advice to stay indoors for safety.

cards.r: jūn zǐ yī yán, sì mǎ nán zhuī
cards.mean: a promise once given must be kept; it can't be taken back
cards.lit: once a gentleman has said a word, even a team of four horses cannot catch it

story.text: The image goes back to the Analects of Confucius. An official named Ji Zicheng said that a gentleman needs only good substance and no refinement. Confucius's disciple Zigong regretted the remark and said that a team of four horses cannot catch the tongue: once words are spoken, they cannot be called back. The later saying turns this into a pledge that a promise, once made, stands.

use.how: Said by the person making a promise, often right after 一言为定, to vouch that they will keep their word; also used to hold someone else to a promise.

near.diff: 一人做事一人当 is taking the consequences of something already done; 君子一言，驷马难追 is standing by a promise made.

cards.cue: You agree to lend your friend your car next weekend. He asks twice whether you really mean it, and you assure him you won't go back on your word.

ctx.s: “说好了，你明天请我吃饭！”“{君子一言，驷马难追}！”
ctx.en: "It's a deal, you're buying me dinner tomorrow!" "I gave my word, and I'll keep it!"

ctx.s: 放心吧，我答应帮你搬家就一定来，{君子一言，驷马难追}。
ctx.en: Don't worry, I said I'd help you move and I'll be there. A promise is a promise.

ctx.s: 你刚才说赢了就请大家喝奶茶，{君子一言，驷马难追}，可不能反悔啊。
ctx.en: You just said you'd buy everyone bubble tea if you won. You gave your word, so no backing out.

ctx.s: 两位老板握着手说：“一言为定，{君子一言，驷马难追}。”
ctx.en: The two bosses shook hands: "It's agreed. Our word is our bond."

ctx.s: 爸爸常说{君子一言，驷马难追}，所以他答应的事从来没有食言过。
ctx.en: Dad often says a promise once made can't be taken back, so he has never broken his word.

ctx.s: 他当年说过一定还这笔钱，十年后果然还清了，真正做到了{君子一言，驷马难追}。
ctx.en: Years ago he said he would pay the money back, and ten years later he did, truly keeping his word.

bad.s: 他的谣言传得很快，真是{君子一言，驷马难追}。
bad.en: (meant: his rumours spread very fast)
bad.why: It is a pledge to keep one's promise, not a remark about words or rumours spreading quickly.

bad.s: 我也不知道明天能不能来，{君子一言，驷马难追}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm not sure whether I can come tomorrow)
bad.why: It backs a firm promise, so it contradicts a vague or uncertain answer.

cards.r: míng rén bù shuō àn huà
cards.mean: let's be frank and say plainly what we mean
cards.lit: a person who acts in the open does not talk in the dark

use.how: Said by the speaker at the start of a frank statement, often before an unwelcome request, refusal or accusation: 明人不说暗话，这件事我不同意。

near.diff: 打开天窗说亮话 invites both sides to drop pretence and talk openly; 明人不说暗话 announces that the speaker is about to be blunt.

cards.cue: Tired of dropping hints about the dirty dishes, you sit your flatmate down and open by announcing that you are about to be blunt with him.

ctx.s: {明人不说暗话}，我觉得你这次做得不对。
ctx.en: I'll be straight with you: I think you got this one wrong.

ctx.s: {明人不说暗话}，这个价格太高了，我们接受不了。
ctx.en: Let's be frank: this price is too high, and we can't accept it.

ctx.s: 老张放下茶杯：“{明人不说暗话}，你是不是想跳槽？”
ctx.en: Lao Zhang put down his tea: "Let's not beat about the bush. Are you thinking of leaving for another job?"

ctx.s: “你到底想说什么？”“{明人不说暗话}，你那份报告错误太多了。”
ctx.en: "What are you trying to say?" "I'll say it plainly: your report has far too many mistakes."

ctx.s: 既然大家都是老朋友了，那就{明人不说暗话}，这个项目我想自己做。
ctx.en: Since we're all old friends, I'll be honest: I want to do this project myself.

ctx.s: 谈判一开始，对方经理就说{明人不说暗话}，直接提出了他们的条件。
ctx.en: Right at the start of the negotiations, the other side's manager said he'd be frank and laid out their terms.

bad.s: 他是个{明人不说暗话}，大家都很喜欢他。
bad.en: (meant: he is a straightforward person and everyone likes him)
bad.why: It is a whole sentence a speaker says before speaking frankly, not a noun for a frank person.

bad.s: 这件事是秘密，{明人不说暗话}，你千万别告诉别人。
bad.en: (meant: this is a secret, don't tell anyone)
bad.why: It announces frankness; it does not mean keeping secrets or not gossiping.

cards.r: léi shēng dà, yǔ diǎn xiǎo
cards.mean: much fanfare at the start, little real action after
cards.lit: loud thunder, tiny raindrops: a storm that roars but hardly rains

use.how: Usually a predicate, often after 又是/总是: 这次整改又是雷声大，雨点小。 Criticises plans, campaigns or threats announced loudly that deliver little.

near.diff: 虎头蛇尾 is starting strong and fizzling out as the work goes on; 雷声大，雨点小 stresses loud announcements or threats followed by little real action.

cards.cue: The company launched a 'green office' drive with posters, slogans and a big kick-off meeting; three months later nothing at all had changed.

ctx.s: 他天天说要减肥，结果还是{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: He talks about losing weight every day, but it's all talk and very little action.

ctx.s: 妈妈每次都说要没收我的手机，可每次都{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: Mum always says she'll confiscate my phone, but it's always a lot of noise and nothing happens.

ctx.s: 公司宣传了半天的新福利，最后只发了一张购物卡，真是{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: The company hyped its new staff benefits for ages, and in the end all we got was one shopping card. So much fanfare for so little.

ctx.s: “上次你说要整顿纪律，怎么又是{雷声大，雨点小}？”同事笑着问经理。
ctx.en: "Last time you said you'd tighten discipline. How come it was all noise again?" a colleague asked the manager with a laugh.

ctx.s: 小区说要彻底清理楼道里的杂物，大家都担心又是{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: The estate announced it would clear all the clutter out of the stairwells, and everyone worried it would be big talk and little action again.

ctx.s: 开会时人人都说要合作，真到出钱出力的时候却{雷声大，雨点小}。
ctx.en: At the meeting everyone talked about working together, but when it came to putting in money and effort, there was little to show for it.

bad.s: 昨天的音乐会{雷声大，雨点小}，观众都特别满意。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday's concert was loud and lively and the audience loved it)
bad.why: It is a criticism of big announcements followed by little action, never praise for a loud or exciting event.

bad.s: 他说话声音很大，做事却很细心，是个{雷声大，雨点小}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he has a loud voice but works carefully)
bad.why: It does not describe a loud voice; it criticises big talk, plans or threats that lead to little real action.

cards.r: zhǐ bāo bu zhù huǒ
cards.mean: the truth can't be covered up for long; it will come out
cards.lit: paper cannot wrap up fire: sooner or later the flame burns through

use.how: A whole clause, often a warning: 纸包不住火，你还是说实话吧。 Said about lies, cover-ups and hidden wrongdoing that will come to light.

near.diff: 此地无银三百两 is a clumsy denial that itself gives the secret away; 纸包不住火 says any concealed fact will come out in time.

cards.cue: A friend has hidden a failed exam from their parents for weeks and plans to keep lying. You warn them it will come out anyway.

ctx.s: 你别再瞒着了，{纸包不住火}，老师迟早会知道的。
ctx.en: Stop hiding it. You can't keep something like this covered up; the teacher will find out sooner or later.

ctx.s: “这件事能瞒多久？”“{纸包不住火}，早点说出来反而好。”
ctx.en: "How long can we keep this quiet?" "Not long; the truth always comes out. It's better to say it early."

ctx.s: 她把车撞坏了却不敢告诉丈夫，可心里清楚{纸包不住火}。
ctx.en: She dented the car and didn't dare tell her husband, but she knew perfectly well he would find out.

ctx.s: 产品有问题就该马上召回，{纸包不住火}，拖下去公司的名声就完了。
ctx.en: If a product is faulty it should be recalled at once. It will come out anyway, and if you stall, the company's reputation is finished.

ctx.s: 他偷偷挪用公款，以为没人发现，可{纸包不住火}，半年后还是被查出来了。
ctx.en: He secretly took company money and thought no one would notice, but it couldn't stay hidden: six months later he was found out.

ctx.s: 那家餐厅用过期食材的事，终究是{纸包不住火}，被一名员工曝光了。
ctx.en: In the end the restaurant couldn't hide its use of expired ingredients; one of its own staff exposed it.

bad.s: 他升职的好消息{纸包不住火}，大家很快就都知道了。
bad.en: (meant: the good news of his promotion spread quickly)
bad.why: It is about a secret or wrongdoing someone tries to hide coming out, not about good news spreading.

bad.s: 她脾气很急，就像{纸包不住火}，一点小事就发火。
bad.en: (meant: she has a hot temper and flares up over little things)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with temper or feelings bursting out; it says a concealed fact cannot stay hidden.

cards.t: 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门
cards.r: bù zuò kuī xīn shì, bù pà guǐ qiāo mén
cards.mean: with a clear conscience you have nothing to fear
cards.lit: do nothing that weighs on your conscience, and you need not fear a ghost knocking at your door

use.how: A whole clause, said by someone suspected or investigated to show they are calm and innocent, or as moral advice: 查就查吧，不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门。

near.diff: 真金不怕火炼 is about real quality surviving a test; 不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门 is about having done nothing wrong and so fearing no investigation.

cards.cue: Auditors arrive and the whole office is nervous, but the accountant calmly opens every book: she has never fiddled a single figure.

ctx.s: 查就查吧，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: Let them check. I've done nothing wrong, so I've nothing to be afraid of.

ctx.s: 有人说他收了回扣，他笑着说：“{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}，随便查。”
ctx.en: Someone claimed he had taken kickbacks. He just smiled: "My conscience is clear. Check whatever you like."

ctx.s: 你要是真没拿那笔钱，怕什么？{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: If you really didn't take the money, what are you afraid of? If you've done nothing wrong, you've nothing to fear.

ctx.s: 警察上门了解情况，老张一点也不慌，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}嘛。
ctx.en: When the police came round asking questions, Lao Zhang wasn't flustered at all. He had nothing on his conscience, after all.

ctx.s: 奶奶常教育我们做人要老实，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: Grandma always taught us to be honest: if you do nothing to be ashamed of, you never have to be afraid.

ctx.s: 公司要公开各部门的账目，别人都紧张，财务主管却很坦然：{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
ctx.en: The company was going to open every department's accounts. Others were nervous, but the finance manager was calm: with a clean record, there was nothing to fear.

bad.s: 他胆子很大，晚上一个人走山路，真是{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
bad.en: (meant: he's brave enough to walk a mountain path alone at night)
bad.why: It is about a clear conscience when facing suspicion, not physical courage or not being scared of the dark.

bad.s: 这次考试我准备得很充分，{不做亏心事，不怕鬼敲门}。
bad.en: (meant: I've prepared well, so I'm not worried about the exam)
bad.why: It means being innocent of wrongdoing; being well prepared for a test has nothing to do with conscience.

cards.r: zhēn jīn bù pà huǒ liàn
cards.mean: what is genuine holds up under any test
cards.lit: real gold does not fear the smelting fire: the heat only proves it is pure

use.how: A whole clause, said when something is doubted or put to a test: 真金不怕火炼，欢迎检测。 Used of products, skill, character or relationships confident of passing scrutiny.

near.diff: 是金子总会发光 says real talent will be noticed sooner or later; 真金不怕火炼 says what is genuine will survive doubt and testing.

cards.cue: A rival claims a small farm's honey is fake. The owner cheerfully sends samples to three independent labs, sure of the results.

ctx.s: 我们的产品质量没问题，{真金不怕火炼}，欢迎检测。
ctx.en: There's nothing wrong with our products. The genuine article can stand any test, so feel free to have them checked.

ctx.s: 这块玉是不是真的，拿去鉴定一下就知道了，{真金不怕火炼}嘛。
ctx.en: Whether this jade is real, a valuation will tell us. If it's genuine, it'll pass.

ctx.s: 有人怀疑他的数据是编的，他只说：“{真金不怕火炼}，你们尽管重做实验。”
ctx.en: Some suspected his data was made up. He simply said: "Real results stand up to anything. Go ahead and repeat the experiment."

ctx.s: 两人的感情经历了异地和失业，{真金不怕火炼}，反而更深了。
ctx.en: Their relationship went through living apart and losing jobs, and like true gold in the fire, it only grew deeper.

ctx.s: 这位选手的实力经过一场场大赛的考验，证明了{真金不怕火炼}。
ctx.en: This player's ability has been tested in one major tournament after another, proving that true quality holds up under pressure.

ctx.s: 面对一轮又一轮的质疑，这位老教授只说了一句：{真金不怕火炼}。
ctx.en: Faced with round after round of doubts, the old professor said only one thing: what is genuine fears no test.

bad.s: 这口锅是铸铁的，{真金不怕火炼}，可以直接放在火上烧。
bad.en: (meant: this pan is cast iron, so it can go straight on the flame)
bad.why: It is figurative, about something genuine passing a test or scrutiny, not about objects that can stand heat.

bad.s: 他刚进公司没多久就被老板看中了，真是{真金不怕火炼}。
bad.en: (meant: his talent was spotted soon after he joined)
bad.why: Being noticed quickly is a different saying; this one needs a doubt or a test that something genuine survives.

cards.r: yī rén zuò shì yī rén dāng
cards.mean: I alone take the consequences of what I did
cards.lit: one person did the deed, so that one person bears it

use.how: A whole clause, usually said by the one responsible to stop others sharing the blame: 是我弄的，一人做事一人当。 Also used as advice to take responsibility.

near.diff: 敢作敢当 describes a person's character as bold and responsible; 一人做事一人当 is said at the moment of owning one specific act.

cards.cue: The whole class is going to be kept in for a broken window. One boy stands up, says he did it alone, and asks that the others go home.

ctx.s: 窗户是我打破的，{一人做事一人当}，别怪他们。
ctx.en: I broke the window. It's on me alone, so don't blame them.

ctx.s: “要不我跟老师说是我干的吧。”“不用，{一人做事一人当}，我自己去说。”
ctx.en: "Shall I tell the teacher it was me?" "No need. I did it, I'll face it. I'll go and tell him myself."

ctx.s: 你已经是大人了，要学会{一人做事一人当}，别总让父母替你收拾。
ctx.en: You're an adult now. You need to learn to own what you do and stop having your parents clean up after you.

ctx.s: 他刮了别人的车，没有开走，而是留了张纸条：“是我刮的，{一人做事一人当}。”
ctx.en: He scraped someone's car and didn't drive off; he left a note: "I scraped it, and I'll take responsibility."

ctx.s: 方案出了错，他主动向老板承认，说{一人做事一人当}，不能让组员背锅。
ctx.en: When the plan went wrong he went to the boss himself, saying the blame was his alone and his team shouldn't carry it.

ctx.s: 武侠小说里的英雄常把{一人做事一人当}挂在嘴边，从不连累朋友。
ctx.en: Heroes in martial-arts novels are always saying they alone will answer for their deeds, and they never drag their friends into trouble.

bad.s: 这个项目太大，我们不能{一人做事一人当}，得分工合作。
bad.en: (meant: the project is too big for one person; we must divide the work)
bad.why: It is about taking the blame for one's own act, not about one person doing all the work.

bad.s: 老板对员工说：“这次成功，{一人做事一人当}，功劳全是你的。”
bad.en: (meant: this success is all your credit)
bad.why: It is about bearing the consequences of a mistake or misdeed, not about who gets the credit for a success.

cards.r: wú shì bù dēng sān bǎo diàn
cards.mean: I only come calling when there is a favour to ask
cards.lit: with no business, one does not climb up to the hall of the Three Jewels

story.text: The Three Jewels (san bao) is the Buddhist name for the Buddha, his teaching (the Dharma) and the community of monks (the Sangha). A 'hall of the Three Jewels' is the hall of a Buddhist temple where they are honoured: a solemn place that people did not wander into idly but visited for a purpose, to pray or ask for help. The saying borrows this to admit, half jokingly, that a visit has a request behind it.
story.source: Buddhist term 三宝 (the Three Jewels)

use.how: A whole clause, said by a visitor of themselves (我今天是无事不登三宝殿) or teasingly by the host (你是无事不登三宝殿吧). Admits a visit comes with a favour to ask.

near.diff: 临时抱佛脚 is scrambling to prepare at the last minute; 无事不登三宝殿 is visiting someone only because you need something from them.

cards.cue: An old classmate you haven't heard from in a year turns up with a bag of fruit, smiles, and admits there's a little something he needs your help with.

ctx.s: 老同学笑着说：“我今天是{无事不登三宝殿}，想请你帮个忙。”
ctx.en: My old classmate said with a smile: "I'll be honest, I haven't come just to chat. I'd like to ask you a favour."

ctx.s: 你平时很少来我这儿，今天是{无事不登三宝殿}吧？说吧，什么事？
ctx.en: You hardly ever drop by, so you must want something today. Go on, what is it?

ctx.s: 邻居提着水果来敲门，我心里明白，他{无事不登三宝殿}。
ctx.en: When my neighbour knocked on the door holding a bag of fruit, I knew he hadn't come for nothing.

ctx.s: 小李一进门就帮经理倒茶，经理笑了：“{无事不登三宝殿}，有话直说吧。”
ctx.en: Xiao Li came in and poured the manager a cup of tea straight away. The manager laughed: "You don't come here without a reason. Out with it."

ctx.s: 这么晚打扰您真不好意思，我也是{无事不登三宝殿}，孩子上学的事想请您指点一下。
ctx.en: Sorry to bother you so late. I wouldn't come without a reason: I'd like your advice about my child's schooling.

ctx.s: 表弟一年没联系，突然请我吃饭，果然是{无事不登三宝殿}，想借我的车。
ctx.en: My cousin hadn't been in touch for a year and suddenly invited me to dinner. Sure enough, he wanted something: to borrow my car.

bad.s: 我奶奶信佛，每个星期都去寺庙，真是{无事不登三宝殿}。
bad.en: (meant: my grandmother is Buddhist and goes to the temple every week)
bad.why: It is not about going to temples; it jokes that someone pays a visit only because they want a favour.

bad.s: 你有空常来玩，我们家{无事不登三宝殿}，随时欢迎！
bad.en: (meant: come round whenever you like, you're always welcome)
bad.why: It says people visit only when they need something, so it cannot serve as a warm open invitation.

cards.r: yuǎn shuǐ jiě bu liǎo jìn kě
cards.mean: help that is far away is no use for an urgent need
cards.lit: far-off water cannot quench a thirst that is close at hand

story.text: Duke Mu of Lu sent his sons to serve at the courts of the powerful states of Jin and Jing (Chu), hoping for their protection. One of his advisers objected: if a child is drowning and you send all the way to Yue for a swimmer, however good, the child will die; if a fire breaks out and you fetch water from the sea, the fire will not go out. Far water does not save you from a near fire. Jin and Jing are strong, but Qi is right next door. The modern saying puts thirst in place of the fire.
story.source: 《韩非子·说林上》 (as 远水不救近火)

use.how: A whole clause, often after 可是/但是: 他答应下个月寄钱，可远水解不了近渴。 Said when help that is promised or distant cannot meet a pressing need.

near.diff: 远亲不如近邻 says neighbours help more than distant relatives; 远水解不了近渴 says any help that is too far off or too late is useless right now.

cards.cue: Your rent is due tomorrow, and the bank says the money your parents sent from abroad will take two weeks to arrive.

ctx.s: 我急着用钱，可父母都在外地，就算想帮忙也是{远水解不了近渴}。
ctx.en: I need money urgently, but my parents live in another city; even if they want to help, they're too far away to do anything now.

ctx.s: 他说下个月发了工资就还我，可我明天就要交房租，{远水解不了近渴}啊。
ctx.en: He says he'll pay me back when he gets paid next month, but my rent is due tomorrow. That's no help now.

ctx.s: “补贴明年才发下来。”“{远水解不了近渴}，店这个月就撑不住了。”
ctx.en: "The subsidy won't be paid until next year." "That's too late to help; the shop won't make it through this month."

ctx.s: 新招的人下个月才到岗，{远水解不了近渴}，这周的活只能我们加班干。
ctx.en: The new hires don't start until next month, which doesn't help us now; we'll have to do overtime to get this week's work done.

ctx.s: 等总部派人来修要三天，{远水解不了近渴}，咱们能不能先找本地的师傅？
ctx.en: Waiting for headquarters to send someone will take three days, and we can't wait that long. Can we find a local repairman first?

ctx.s: 暴雨冲断了公路，救援物资还在几十公里外，{远水解不了近渴}，村民们只好互相帮助。
ctx.en: The storm washed out the road and the relief supplies were still dozens of kilometres away, too far to help, so the villagers had to rely on each other.

bad.s: 我渴极了，可是{远水解不了近渴}，就去买了一瓶水。
bad.en: (meant: I was really thirsty, so I bought a bottle of water)
bad.why: It is figurative, about distant or late help for an urgent problem, not about actually being thirsty.

bad.s: 他住得离我很远，我们{远水解不了近渴}，很少见面。
bad.en: (meant: he lives far from me, so we rarely meet)
bad.why: It is not about friends living far apart; it says help that arrives from afar or too late can't meet an urgent need.

cards.r: wū lòu piān féng lián yè yǔ
cards.mean: misfortune piles on when you are already in trouble
cards.lit: the roof is leaking, and just then it rains night after night

use.how: A whole clause, a sigh over bad luck, usually with both blows named: 真是屋漏偏逢连夜雨，刚丢了工作又生了病。

near.diff: 雪上加霜 is a four-character comment that something made a bad situation worse; 屋漏偏逢连夜雨 is a full, sighing saying about bad luck hitting when you're already down.

cards.cue: The day after a man loses his job, his car breaks down and his landlord announces a rent rise.

ctx.s: 我刚丢了钱包，手机又摔坏了，真是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
ctx.en: I'd just lost my wallet, and then I broke my phone too. When it rains, it pours.

ctx.s: “你脸色怎么这么差？”“别提了，{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}，感冒还没好又扭了脚。”
ctx.en: "Why do you look so awful?" "Don't ask. One thing after another: I'm not over my cold yet and now I've twisted my ankle."

ctx.s: 赶飞机已经晚了，路上偏偏又堵车，这不是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}吗？
ctx.en: I was already late for my flight, and then I got stuck in traffic. Isn't that just bad luck piling on?

ctx.s: 公司本来就在亏钱，最大的客户又走了，{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}啊。
ctx.en: The company was already losing money, and now its biggest client has left. Trouble on top of trouble.

ctx.s: 那年家里的小店刚倒闭，父亲又住了院，{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}，日子特别难。
ctx.en: That year our family's little shop had just closed down when Dad was taken into hospital. Misfortune kept piling on, and life was very hard.

ctx.s: 球队本就有两名主力受伤，赛前一晚队长又发起高烧，可谓{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
ctx.en: The team already had two key players injured, and on the eve of the match the captain came down with a high fever: one blow after another.

bad.s: 我考上了大学，又中了奖，真是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
bad.en: (meant: I got into university and won a prize, two pieces of good luck)
bad.why: It is only for misfortune piling up; two pieces of good news at once calls for a different saying.

bad.s: 我的手机屏幕裂了，真是{屋漏偏逢连夜雨}。
bad.en: (meant: my phone screen cracked, what bad luck)
bad.why: One mishap alone does not fit; it needs a fresh blow landing on top of trouble that was already there.

cards.t: 留得青山在，不怕没柴烧
cards.r: liú de qīng shān zài, bù pà méi chái shāo
cards.mean: as long as the essentials survive, there is hope to recover
cards.lit: keep the green hills standing, and you'll never run short of firewood to burn

use.how: A whole clause of advice or comfort after a loss or before a sacrifice: 钱没了可以再挣，留得青山在，不怕没柴烧。 Says protect what matters most, rebuild later.

near.diff: 车到山前必有路 says a way out will turn up by itself; 留得青山在，不怕没柴烧 says to protect what matters most, such as health, so you can recover.

cards.cue: A friend's restaurant has failed and he wants to keep working while ill to pay off debts. You tell him to get his health back first; he can always start again.

ctx.s: 生意没了可以再做，身体最要紧，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
ctx.en: You can always start another business; your health is what matters most. As long as you're well, you can rebuild.

ctx.s: 你现在硬撑下去，万一累倒了怎么办？{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}啊。
ctx.en: If you push on like this and collapse, what then? Keep yourself in one piece and there will be other chances.

ctx.s: 公司决定卖掉两家分店，保住总店，老板说：“{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。”
ctx.en: The company decided to sell two branches to save the main store. The boss said: "As long as the core survives, we can grow again."

ctx.s: 一场大火烧了仓库，好在没人受伤，爷爷说{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
ctx.en: A fire destroyed the warehouse, but luckily no one was hurt. Grandpa said that as long as we're all alive and well, we can build everything up again.

ctx.s: 别为了一次升职把身体熬垮了，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}嘛。
ctx.en: Don't wear yourself out for one promotion. Stay healthy and there'll be plenty more opportunities.

ctx.s: 球队虽然输了决赛，但核心队员都还在，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}，明年再来。
ctx.en: The team lost the final, but its core players are all staying. With the essentials intact, they can come back and try again next year.

bad.s: 我们去山里砍柴吧，{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
bad.en: (meant: let's go and collect firewood in the hills)
bad.why: It is figurative comfort or advice about loss and recovery, not a remark about hills or firewood.

bad.s: 他已经很有钱了，还在拼命赚钱，真是{留得青山在，不怕没柴烧}。
bad.en: (meant: he's already rich and still works himself hard for money)
bad.why: It is said after a setback to save the essentials for later, not to describe someone greedy or hard-working.

cards.r: sǐ mǎ dàng huó mǎ yī
cards.mean: to try anything anyway, though the case looks hopeless
cards.lit: to treat a dead horse as though it were still alive

use.how: Usually a predicate, often with 只好/就 or ending in 吧: 只好死马当活马医了。 Said, with a wry shrug, of trying a last unlikely fix because nothing else is left.

near.diff: 病急乱投医 criticises grabbing at any help in a panic; 死马当活马医 is a knowing last try, made while expecting little.

cards.cue: Two repair shops say your old laptop is beyond saving, but before throwing it out you try a random fix you saw in a video anyway.

ctx.s: 这台电脑反正修不好了，我就{死马当活马医}，自己拆开看看。
ctx.en: This computer can't be repaired anyway, so I'll give it a go myself and open it up. Nothing to lose.

ctx.s: “这个办法能行吗？”“不知道，{死马当活马医}吧。”
ctx.en: "Will this work?" "No idea. It's a long shot, but we've got nothing to lose."

ctx.s: 那盆花眼看要枯死了，妈妈说{死马当活马医}，给它换了新土。
ctx.en: The plant was about to die, so Mum said we might as well try anything and repotted it in fresh soil.

ctx.s: 车在半路熄了火，附近又没有修车店，他只好{死马当活马医}，照着说明书一项项检查。
ctx.en: The car stalled halfway and there was no garage nearby, so with nothing else to try he went through the manual item by item.

ctx.s: 项目眼看要失败，经理决定{死马当活马医}，让新来的实习生试试他的想法。
ctx.en: With the project about to fail, the manager decided there was nothing to lose and let the new intern try out his idea.

ctx.s: 球队落后三球，教练{死马当活马医}，最后十分钟把所有前锋都换上了场。
ctx.en: Three goals down, the coach threw caution to the wind and sent on every striker he had for the last ten minutes.

bad.s: 这位兽医对每只小动物都{死马当活马医}，非常细心负责。
bad.en: (meant: this vet treats every little animal with great care)
bad.why: It is a wry last try on a case already given up as hopeless, not praise for careful, dedicated treatment.

bad.s: 这道题很简单，我{死马当活马医}，五分钟就做完了。
bad.en: (meant: the problem was easy and I solved it in five minutes)
bad.why: It only fits a case that already looks hopeless; using it for an easy task makes no sense.

cards.r: hǎo hàn bù chī yǎn qián kuī
cards.mean: a sensible person backs down rather than lose out on the spot
cards.lit: a real man of courage does not take a beating right in front of his eyes

use.how: A full sentence, often to justify giving in when facing someone stronger: 算了，好汉不吃眼前亏。 Said about yielding, apologising or paying up rather than losing a face-off.

near.diff: 走为上计 means getting away; 好汉不吃眼前亏 means giving in on the spot, for example by apologising or handing something over.

near.t: 留得青山在，不怕没柴烧
near.diff: 留得青山在 is about saving your strength after a big setback; 好汉不吃眼前亏 is about yielding in an immediate confrontation.

cards.cue: Three big drunk men block your way and demand an apology for a bump that was their fault. You apologise anyway, and later tell your friend why.

ctx.s: 对方人多，你就先认个错吧，{好汉不吃眼前亏}。
ctx.en: There are more of them, so just say sorry for now. No sense getting hurt over it.

ctx.s: 他明明没错，却低头道了歉，事后说：“{好汉不吃眼前亏}嘛。”
ctx.en: He wasn't in the wrong, but he apologised anyway, and afterwards said: "Why take a beating on the spot?"

ctx.s: 小偷亮出了刀，他想到{好汉不吃眼前亏}，就把钱包交了出去。
ctx.en: When the thief pulled out a knife, he decided it wasn't worth getting hurt and handed over his wallet.

ctx.s: “你怎么不跟老板理论？”“他正在气头上，{好汉不吃眼前亏}，以后再说。”
ctx.en: "Why didn't you argue with the boss?" "He's furious right now. No point getting burned; I'll bring it up later."

ctx.s: 对方占尽了优势，经理心想{好汉不吃眼前亏}，先让了一步。
ctx.en: The other side held all the cards, so the manager thought it wiser to back down and give a little ground for now.

ctx.s: 爷爷常说，{好汉不吃眼前亏}，硬碰硬只会让自己受伤。
ctx.en: Grandpa always says a wise man doesn't take a loss he can avoid; meeting force with force only gets you hurt.

bad.s: 我昨天吃了很多亏，真是{好汉不吃眼前亏}。
bad.en: (meant: I lost out a lot yesterday)
bad.why: It is advice to back down so as to avoid a loss, not a description of having suffered one.

bad.s: 他面对困难从不退缩，真是{好汉不吃眼前亏}。
bad.en: (meant: he never backs off from difficulty, a true hero)
bad.why: The saying justifies backing down, so it cannot praise someone for standing firm.

cards.r: sān shí liù jì, zǒu wéi shàng jì
cards.mean: when there is no way to win, getting away is the best plan
cards.lit: of the thirty-six stratagems, walking away is the best one

story.text: In the Southern Qi dynasty the general Wang Jingze rose in revolt. Hearing that the crown prince had packed up and was ready to flee, he mocked them: of Lord Tan's thirty-six stratagems, running away was the best, so father and son had better run at once. Lord Tan was Tan Daoji, a general of the earlier Liu Song dynasty remembered for withdrawing his army from the Northern Wei. The famous book called the Thirty-Six Stratagems was compiled much later.

use.how: A full sentence, often jokingly, when someone decides to slip away from a bad or awkward situation: 情况不妙，三十六计，走为上计。

near.diff: 好汉不吃眼前亏 means yielding to avoid a loss on the spot; 走为上计 means physically leaving or escaping.

cards.cue: The host's uncle has started his third long speech of the evening. You and a friend exchange a look and quietly head for the door.

ctx.s: 看到妈妈拿着成绩单走过来，弟弟心想：{三十六计，走为上计}。
ctx.en: Seeing Mum coming over with his report card, my little brother thought: time to make a run for it.

ctx.s: 酒桌上大家又开始劝酒，我说：“{三十六计，走为上计}，先走一步！”
ctx.en: When everyone started pushing drinks again, I said: "The best plan is a quick exit. I'll be off first!"

ctx.s: “那个推销员又来了！”“快，{三十六计，走为上计}！”
ctx.en: "That salesman's coming back!" "Quick, let's get out of here!"

ctx.s: 敌人太多，硬拼没有胜算，将军下令：{三十六计，走为上计}。
ctx.en: The enemy far outnumbered them and a fight could not be won, so the general ordered a retreat: getting away was the best plan.

ctx.s: 明知这场争论赢不了，他用了{三十六计，走为上计}这一招，找借口离开了会场。
ctx.en: Knowing he couldn't win the argument, he used the oldest trick there is: he made an excuse and left the meeting.

ctx.s: 公司已经半年发不出工资了，{三十六计，走为上计}，他开始找新工作。
ctx.en: The company hadn't paid wages for half a year. Getting out was the best move, so he started looking for a new job.

bad.s: 今天天气很好，{三十六计，走为上计}，我们去公园散步吧。
bad.en: (meant: the weather is nice, let's go for a walk in the park)
bad.why: The "going" here means escaping trouble you cannot win, not going out for a walk.

bad.s: 这次考试我准备了很多方法，{三十六计，走为上计}。
bad.en: (meant: I have prepared lots of strategies for this exam)
bad.why: It does not praise having many plans; it says that the best plan of all is to run away.

cards.r: yī shān bù róng èr hǔ
cards.mean: two strong rivals cannot share one place of power
cards.lit: one mountain cannot hold two tigers

use.how: A full sentence or after 真是, said about two strong people competing for the same top position, where one must go: 两个人都想当老大，一山不容二虎。

cards.cue: After a merger, two star managers are both promised the director's job. Within a month one of them resigns, and nobody is surprised.

ctx.s: 两个队长都想说了算，{一山不容二虎}，球队天天吵架。
ctx.en: Both captains wanted to be in charge. There wasn't room for two of them, and the team argued every day.

ctx.s: 公司合并后，两位总经理只能留一位，{一山不容二虎}嘛。
ctx.en: After the merger only one of the two general managers could stay. There's no room for two at the top.

ctx.s: “他们俩怎么总是对着干？”“都想当老大呗，{一山不容二虎}。”
ctx.en: "Why are those two always at each other's throats?" "They both want to be top dog. One mountain can't hold two tigers."

ctx.s: 两只公猫在一个家里天天打架，真是{一山不容二虎}。
ctx.en: The two tomcats fight every day in the same house. There really isn't room for both of them.

ctx.s: 乐队里有两个都想当主唱的明星，{一山不容二虎}，乐队很快就解散了。
ctx.en: The band had two stars who both wanted to be lead singer. Neither would give way, and the band soon broke up.

ctx.s: 历史上很多联盟最后破裂，原因往往是{一山不容二虎}。
ctx.en: Many alliances in history eventually fell apart, often because two strong leaders could not share power.

bad.s: 我家有两只猫，{一山不容二虎}，它们关系很好。
bad.en: (meant: we have two cats and they get on well)
bad.why: It says two rivals cannot live side by side, so it cannot describe two who get along.

bad.s: 他一个人做两份工作，真是{一山不容二虎}。
bad.en: (meant: he can't manage two jobs at once)
bad.why: It is about two strong rivals for one position, not one person juggling two tasks.

cards.r: yī gè bā zhang pāi bu xiǎng
cards.mean: it takes two to quarrel; both sides share the blame
cards.lit: one palm on its own cannot make a clap

use.how: A full sentence, said after a quarrel or fight to refuse to blame only one side: 吵架这种事，一个巴掌拍不响。

cards.cue: Two children run to their mother, each insisting the other started the fight. Without asking who hit first, she sends both to their rooms.

ctx.s: 你们俩打架，{一个巴掌拍不响}，都有错。
ctx.en: You two were fighting. It takes two, so you're both in the wrong.

ctx.s: 妈妈不听哥哥解释，只说：“{一个巴掌拍不响}，你们俩都去罚站。”
ctx.en: Mum wouldn't listen to my brother's excuses and just said: "It takes two to fight. Both of you, go and stand in the corner."

ctx.s: “都是他不讲理！”“{一个巴掌拍不响}，你就一点问题都没有吗？”
ctx.en: "It's all because he's unreasonable!" "It takes two to quarrel. Are you saying you did nothing wrong at all?"

ctx.s: 夫妻吵架，{一个巴掌拍不响}，别只怪你老公一个人。
ctx.en: When a couple fights, it takes two. Don't just blame your husband.

ctx.s: 邻居们都说是他先动手，可我觉得{一个巴掌拍不响}。
ctx.en: The neighbours all say he threw the first punch, but I think both sides played a part.

ctx.s: 两个部门的矛盾闹了很久，领导认为{一个巴掌拍不响}，让双方都写检讨。
ctx.en: The feud between the two departments had dragged on for ages. The boss decided both were to blame and had each side write a self-criticism.

bad.s: 他在路上被一个陌生人无故打了，真是{一个巴掌拍不响}。
bad.en: (meant: he was hit by a stranger for no reason)
bad.why: It shares the blame between both sides, so it cannot describe an unprovoked attack on an innocent person.

bad.s: 他一句话也不说，教室里安静极了，真是{一个巴掌拍不响}。
bad.en: (meant: he said nothing and the classroom was completely silent)
bad.why: The missing clap is only an image; the saying is about a conflict having two sides, not about silence.

cards.r: qiǎng niǔ de guā bù tián
cards.mean: a relationship or deal that is forced never turns out well
cards.lit: a melon twisted off the vine by force, before it is ripe, is not sweet

use.how: A full sentence, used as advice against forcing a match, a job or a deal on someone unwilling: 他不愿意就算了，强扭的瓜不甜。

near.diff: 天涯何处无芳草 comforts someone after losing a partner; 强扭的瓜不甜 warns against forcing someone who is unwilling.

cards.cue: Parents keep pushing their son to marry a family friend's daughter, though the two have nothing to say to each other. An aunt tells them to stop.

ctx.s: 她不喜欢你，别再追了，{强扭的瓜不甜}。
ctx.en: She doesn't like you, so stop chasing her. You can't force these things.

ctx.s: 孩子对钢琴一点兴趣都没有，你逼他学也没用，{强扭的瓜不甜}。
ctx.en: The child has no interest in the piano at all. Forcing him won't help; nothing good comes of it.

ctx.s: “他要是不愿意来我们公司，就别勉强了。”“对，{强扭的瓜不甜}。”
ctx.en: "If he doesn't want to join our company, let's not push him." "Right, forcing it never works."

ctx.s: 父母硬让他们结婚，结果天天吵架，真是{强扭的瓜不甜}。
ctx.en: Their parents made them marry, and now they quarrel every day. A forced match never turns out well.

ctx.s: 合作要双方自愿，{强扭的瓜不甜}，对方不同意就算了。
ctx.en: A partnership has to be willing on both sides. If they don't agree, let it go; a forced deal is never a good one.

ctx.s: 他把不想留下的员工都放走了，说{强扭的瓜不甜}。
ctx.en: He let every employee who didn't want to stay leave, saying there was no point keeping people against their will.

bad.s: 这家店的水果不新鲜，真是{强扭的瓜不甜}。
bad.en: (meant: this shop's fruit isn't fresh)
bad.why: The melon is only an image; the saying is about forcing an unwilling person, not about the quality of fruit.

bad.s: 他努力了很多年才考上大学，{强扭的瓜不甜}。
bad.en: (meant: he got into university after years of hard work)
bad.why: It warns against forcing someone else's will, not about one's own effort or how hard a goal was to reach.

cards.r: tiān yá hé chù wú fāng cǎo
cards.mean: after a breakup: there are plenty of others out there to love
cards.lit: where, to the ends of the earth, is there no fragrant grass?

story.text: The line comes from a ci poem by the Song poet Su Shi, written to the tune Butterflies Love Flowers, on a spring scene. Late in spring the willow catkins have blown from the branches and grow fewer, and the poet observes that fragrant grass grows everywhere, to the ends of the earth. Later speakers took the fragrant grass to stand for a person to love, and the line became the standard comfort for the heartbroken.

use.how: A full sentence, often followed by 何必单恋一枝花, said to console someone after a breakup or rejection: 别难过了，天涯何处无芳草。

near.diff: 强扭的瓜不甜 warns against forcing someone unwilling; 天涯何处无芳草 comforts someone that there are others to love.

cards.cue: Your best friend was dumped and has stayed in his room for a week. You drag him out to dinner and tell him she is not the only person in the world.

ctx.s: 别哭了，{天涯何处无芳草}，你会遇到更好的人。
ctx.en: Don't cry. There are plenty more fish in the sea; you'll meet someone better.

ctx.s: “她拒绝我了。”“{天涯何处无芳草}，下一个更好！”
ctx.en: "She turned me down." "There are plenty of others out there. The next one will be even better!"

ctx.s: 失恋以后，朋友们都劝他：“{天涯何处无芳草}，何必单恋一枝花？”
ctx.en: After the breakup his friends all told him: "There are plenty of flowers in the world; why pine for just one?"

ctx.s: 表姐离婚后很难过，妈妈安慰她说{天涯何处无芳草}。
ctx.en: My cousin was devastated after her divorce, and Mum comforted her by saying there are plenty of other people out there.

ctx.s: 他嘴上说着{天涯何处无芳草}，心里却还忘不了她。
ctx.en: He kept saying there were plenty of other girls out there, but deep down he still couldn't forget her.

ctx.s: 苏轼的“{天涯何处无芳草}”，本来写的是暮春的景色。
ctx.en: Su Shi's line about fragrant grass everywhere was originally a description of late spring.

bad.s: 他们结婚五十年了，感情很好，真是{天涯何处无芳草}。
bad.en: (meant: they have been happily married for fifty years)
bad.why: It consoles someone who has lost a partner by saying there are others; it cannot praise a lasting marriage.

bad.s: 你妻子刚去世，别太伤心，{天涯何处无芳草}。
bad.en: (meant: to comfort a man whose wife has just died)
bad.why: It is a light comfort for a breakup; said to someone in mourning it sounds heartless and offensive.

cards.t: 千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重
cards.r: qiān lǐ sòng é máo, lǐ qīng qíng yì zhòng
cards.mean: a small gift is precious for the thought behind it
cards.lit: a goose feather sent from a thousand li away: the gift is light, but the feeling behind it is heavy

story.text: A legend tells of Mian Bogao, an envoy sent by the Huihe (Uighur) ruler with a white swan as a gift for Emperor Taizong of Tang. On the long road he stopped at a lake to let the swan bathe, and it flew off, leaving only a feather. Not daring to arrive empty-handed, he presented the feather with a short poem saying the gift was light but the feeling was heavy. The emperor was moved and did not blame him.
story.source: a folk legend set at the Tang court

use.how: A full sentence, said modestly by a giver about a small gift, or warmly by a receiver: 一点小东西，千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重。 Often shortened to 礼轻情意重.

cards.cue: A friend back from her hometown brings you a small jar of her grandmother's homemade chilli sauce and apologises that it's nothing much.

ctx.s: 这是我自己做的小卡片，{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}。
ctx.en: This is a little card I made myself. It's not much, but it comes from the heart.

ctx.s: “这么点东西，不好意思。”“哪里，{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}！”
ctx.en: "Sorry it's such a small thing." "Not at all, it's the thought that counts!"

ctx.s: 老朋友专门从老家带来一包茶叶，{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}，我很感动。
ctx.en: My old friend brought me a packet of tea all the way from his hometown. A small gift, but I was really touched by the thought.

ctx.s: 在国外留学的学生寄来一张明信片，老师笑着说：“{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}啊。”
ctx.en: A former student studying abroad sent a postcard, and the teacher smiled: "A small gift from far away, but what a kind thought."

ctx.s: 送礼不一定要贵，{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}，心意最重要。
ctx.en: A present doesn't have to be expensive. Even a small gift is precious; it's the thought that matters most.

ctx.s: 孩子们用零花钱给奶奶买了一条围巾，奶奶说这就是{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}。
ctx.en: The children bought Grandma a scarf with their pocket money, and she said that was exactly what a small gift with a big heart means.

bad.s: 他送了我一辆新车，真是{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}。
bad.en: (meant: he gave me a new car, how generous)
bad.why: It is about a small, cheap gift; an expensive present like a car is the opposite of light.

bad.s: 他只送了我一支笔，真是{千里送鹅毛，礼轻情意重}，太小气了。
bad.en: (meant: he only gave me a pen, how stingy)
bad.why: It values a small gift for its thought, so it cannot be used to complain that someone is mean.

cards.t: 在家靠父母，出门靠朋友
cards.r: zài jiā kào fù mǔ, chū mén kào péng you
cards.mean: away from home, you have to rely on friends for help
cards.lit: at home you rely on your parents; once you leave home you rely on your friends

use.how: A full sentence, said when living or working far from home: to thank people who helped, to ask for help, or to advise making friends: 在家靠父母，出门靠朋友嘛。

near.diff: 远亲不如近邻 says neighbours nearby help more than distant relatives; 在家靠父母，出门靠朋友 is about needing friends once you leave home.

cards.cue: You have just moved to a new city for work and know no one. A classmate's cousin helps you carry your furniture and shows you around. You thank him.

ctx.s: 刚到北京时，多亏同学帮忙，真是{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}。
ctx.en: When I first got to Beijing, my classmates helped me so much. Away from home, you really do depend on friends.

ctx.s: “以后有事尽管找我。”“太好了，{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}嘛！”
ctx.en: "If you ever need anything, just ask me." "Great! Away from home, friends are all you've got!"

ctx.s: 爸爸送我上火车时叮嘱：“{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}，要和同学搞好关系。”
ctx.en: Seeing me off at the train, Dad told me: "Away from home you'll need your friends, so get on well with your classmates."

ctx.s: 他在国外生病时，是几个朋友轮流照顾他，{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}啊。
ctx.en: When he fell ill abroad, a few friends took turns looking after him. Far from home, friends are your family.

ctx.s: 新来的同事请大家吃饭，说：“{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}，以后请多关照！”
ctx.en: The new colleague treated everyone to dinner and said: "Away from home I'll be relying on you all, so please look out for me!"

ctx.s: 在外地打工的老乡们常常互相帮忙，因为大家都明白{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}。
ctx.en: People from the same hometown working far away often help each other out, because they all know that away from home you depend on friends.

bad.s: 我第一次去朋友家玩，{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}。
bad.en: (meant: I visited a friend's home for the first time)
bad.why: "Going out" here means living away from home, and the saying is about needing help; it does not describe a visit.

bad.s: 他从来不帮朋友，因为{在家靠父母，出门靠朋友}。
bad.en: (meant: he never helps his friends)
bad.why: The saying stresses that friends must help each other away from home, so it cannot excuse refusing to help.

cards.r: yī huí shēng, èr huí shú
cards.mean: awkward the first time, at ease the second: familiarity comes fast
cards.lit: a stranger the first time, familiar the second time

use.how: A full sentence, said to put someone at ease when meeting people or doing something for the first time: 别紧张，一回生，二回熟。

near.diff: 万事开头难 stresses that starting is hard; 一回生，二回熟 reassures that it already feels easy the next time.

cards.cue: A shy new neighbour barely speaks at your first dinner together. As you see him out, you tell him that next time it will feel like visiting old friends.

ctx.s: 第一次见面有点紧张很正常，{一回生，二回熟}嘛。
ctx.en: It's normal to be a bit nervous the first time you meet. Next time you'll feel at home.

ctx.s: “我不会用这台机器。”“没关系，{一回生，二回熟}，多用几次就会了。”
ctx.en: "I don't know how to use this machine." "No problem. It's only strange the first time; use it a few times and you'll have it."

ctx.s: 他第一次包饺子包得很难看，奶奶笑着说{一回生，二回熟}。
ctx.en: His first dumplings looked terrible, and Grandma laughed and said he'd get the hang of it next time.

ctx.s: 新来的同事有点拘谨，老张拍拍他的肩说：“{一回生，二回熟}，以后就是自己人了。”
ctx.en: The new colleague was a bit stiff, so Lao Zhang patted him on the shoulder: "First time's always awkward. From now on you're one of us."

ctx.s: 我们第一次合作还不太默契，不过{一回生，二回熟}，下次一定更顺利。
ctx.en: Our first project together wasn't very smooth, but now that we know each other, next time will go much better.

ctx.s: 第一次去那家医院找了半天，{一回生，二回熟}，现在我很快就能找到科室。
ctx.en: The first time I went to that hospital I spent ages looking around, but once you've been there it's easy; now I find the right department in no time.

bad.s: 我们是二十年的老朋友了，真是{一回生，二回熟}。
bad.en: (meant: we have been close friends for twenty years)
bad.why: It is about the first awkward meetings becoming easy, not about a friendship that is already long and deep.

bad.s: 这道菜我做了很多次，还是很生，{一回生，二回熟}。
bad.en: (meant: I've cooked this dish many times and it's still underdone)
bad.why: The words for raw and cooked here mean unfamiliar and familiar; the saying is not about food being undercooked.

cards.r: bù dǎ bù xiāng shí
cards.mean: a clash or fight can be the start of a friendship
cards.lit: without a fight, they would never have come to know each other

story.text: In the novel Water Margin, the hot-tempered Li Kui picks a fight with the fishmonger Zhang Shun on the bank of the Xunyang River. Li Kui beats him on land, but Zhang Shun lures him into the water and nearly drowns him. Song Jiang and Dai Zong step in and introduce the two, and Dai Zong quotes a common saying, in the slightly longer form "bu da bu cheng xiangshi": without a fight, no friendship. From then on the two are firm friends.

use.how: A full sentence or after 真是 or 这叫, said by or about people who became friends after a quarrel or fight: 我们俩是不打不相识。

cards.cue: Two drivers have a minor crash and shout at each other, then discover they come from the same small town. Now they go fishing together every weekend.

ctx.s: 我和他小时候打过一架，后来成了好朋友，真是{不打不相识}。
ctx.en: He and I had a fight as kids and then became best friends. Sometimes a fight is how friendships start.

ctx.s: “你们俩是怎么认识的？”“说来好笑，是吵架吵出来的，{不打不相识}嘛。”
ctx.en: "How did you two meet?" "Funny story, it started with a row. We only became friends because we fought!"

ctx.s: 他和邻居因为停车位吵过一次，没想到{不打不相识}，现在常常一起喝茶。
ctx.en: He once had a row with his neighbour over a parking space; who'd have thought it would make them friends? Now they often have tea together.

ctx.s: 两个球员在场上发生冲突，赛后却握手拥抱，真是{不打不相识}。
ctx.en: The two players clashed on the pitch, but after the game they shook hands and hugged. A fight can be the start of a friendship.

ctx.s: 网上争论过的两个人后来见了面，笑着说彼此是{不打不相识}。
ctx.en: Two people who had argued online later met in person and laughed that their quarrel was how they became friends.

ctx.s: 两家公司打了三年官司，最后却成了合作伙伴，这叫{不打不相识}。
ctx.en: The two companies fought each other in court for three years and ended up as partners. That's how a clash turns into a friendship.

bad.s: 我们俩天天打架，一直合不来，真是{不打不相识}。
bad.en: (meant: we fight every day and have never got on)
bad.why: The clash must lead to friendship; it cannot describe two people who stay enemies.

bad.s: 我和他第一次见面就很投缘，{不打不相识}。
bad.en: (meant: we hit it off the moment we met)
bad.why: There must be a conflict first; without a clash the saying does not apply.

cards.r: yǒu qí fù bì yǒu qí zǐ
cards.mean: like father, like son: children take after their parents
cards.lit: where there is such a father, there is bound to be such a son

use.how: Said as a comment on a child who shows a parent's talent, habit or fault: 真是有其父必有其子。 It can be praise or a dig, depending on the trait.

near.diff: 上梁不正下梁歪 blames juniors' bad behaviour on a bad example from above; 有其父必有其子 just notes that a child resembles a parent, for good or ill.

cards.cue: At a party, a famous chef's twelve-year-old son cooks a dish every bit as good as his dad's. What do the guests remark?

ctx.s: 儿子跟他爸一样爱踢足球，真是{有其父必有其子}。
ctx.en: His son loves football just as much as he does. Like father, like son.

ctx.s: 他爸爸是有名的医生，他也考上了医学院，{有其父必有其子}啊。
ctx.en: His father is a well-known doctor, and he got into medical school too. Like father, like son.

ctx.s: “这孩子说话的样子跟他爸一模一样！”“{有其父必有其子}嘛。”
ctx.en: "The way this kid talks is exactly like his dad!" "Well, like father, like son."

ctx.s: 老张年轻时脾气就急，现在儿子也这样，邻居都说{有其父必有其子}。
ctx.en: Old Zhang had a quick temper when he was young, and now his son is the same; the neighbours all say the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

ctx.s: 小王跟他父亲一样，一聊起钓鱼就停不下来，同事们笑着说：“{有其父必有其子}。”
ctx.en: Just like his father, Xiao Wang can't stop once he starts talking about fishing; his colleagues laugh and say: "Like father, like son."

ctx.s: 报道写道，这位年轻棋手的父亲也曾是全国冠军，可谓{有其父必有其子}。
ctx.en: The report noted that the young chess player's father had also been a national champion: truly like father, like son.

bad.s: 我和我哥长得很像，{有其父必有其子}。
bad.en: (meant: my brother and I look very alike)
bad.why: It is about a child taking after a parent, not about brothers or sisters resembling each other.

bad.s: 他爸爸很高，他却很矮，真是{有其父必有其子}。
bad.en: (meant: his father is tall, but he is short)
bad.why: The saying states a resemblance, so it cannot describe a son who is the opposite of his father.

cards.r: shǒu xīn shǒu bèi dōu shì ròu
cards.mean: they are all equally dear to me; I can't favour one over another
cards.lit: the palm and the back of the hand are both my own flesh

use.how: Said, usually by a parent, when pressed to choose between or favour one of several people equally close to them: 手心手背都是肉，我哪个都舍不得。

cards.cue: A mother of two sons is asked which one she loves more, and she refuses to choose between them. What does she say?

ctx.s: 两个孩子我都爱，{手心手背都是肉}。
ctx.en: I love both my children; they're equally dear to me.

ctx.s: 你问我更疼哪个孙子？{手心手背都是肉}，哪能分得出来！
ctx.en: You're asking which grandson I dote on more? They're both my flesh and blood; how could I pick?

ctx.s: 姐妹俩吵架，妈妈谁也不想偏向，只能叹气：“{手心手背都是肉}啊。”
ctx.en: The two sisters were quarrelling and their mother didn't want to take sides; she could only sigh: "You're both my children."

ctx.s: 爸爸要把房子留给哪个儿子，一直下不了决心，毕竟{手心手背都是肉}。
ctx.en: Dad could never decide which son to leave the house to; after all, he loved them both the same.

ctx.s: 两个都是我带出来的徒弟，{手心手背都是肉}，让我只选一个，太难了。
ctx.en: I trained both of these apprentices myself; they're equally dear to me, and asking me to pick just one is too hard.

ctx.s: 老师说，班里的学生对她来说{手心手背都是肉}，不会偏向成绩好的。
ctx.en: The teacher said every student in her class is equally dear to her, and she won't favour the ones with good grades.

bad.s: 这两家餐厅{手心手背都是肉}，你随便选吧。
bad.en: (meant: both restaurants are equally good, pick either)
bad.why: It is about people you love equally, usually your own children, not about two equally good options.

bad.s: 他把钱都给了大儿子，真是{手心手背都是肉}。
bad.en: (meant: he gave all the money to his eldest son)
bad.why: The saying claims equal love and is used to refuse favouritism, so it cannot describe favouring one child.

cards.r: jiā chǒu bù kě wài yáng
cards.mean: a family's shameful affairs should not be told to outsiders
cards.lit: a family's ugly matters must not be spread outside

use.how: Given as a reason to keep a family's, or by extension a group's, embarrassing problems from outsiders: 这事家丑不可外扬。 Also quoted critically when it is used to hide wrongdoing.

cards.cue: Your uncle has run up big gambling debts, and your mother warns you not to breathe a word of it to the neighbours. What principle does she invoke?

ctx.s: 爸妈吵架的事别跟同学说，{家丑不可外扬}。
ctx.en: Don't tell your classmates that Mum and Dad were fighting. What happens in the family stays in the family.

ctx.s: 奶奶总说{家丑不可外扬}，家里有矛盾从来不让外人知道。
ctx.en: Grandma always says family shame stays at home; she never lets outsiders know about any trouble in the family.

ctx.s: “你哥欠钱的事要不要告诉邻居？”“算了吧，{家丑不可外扬}。”
ctx.en: "Should we tell the neighbours about your brother's debts?" "Better not. You don't air the family's dirty laundry."

ctx.s: 公司内部出了问题，老板却想着{家丑不可外扬}，要求员工不准对外透露。
ctx.en: There was trouble inside the company, but the boss wanted to keep it in-house and told staff not to say a word outside.

ctx.s: 她犹豫了很久才开口，毕竟{家丑不可外扬}，可这次她实在忍不下去了。
ctx.en: She hesitated a long time before speaking up; you don't air family troubles, after all, but this time she just couldn't bear it any more.

ctx.s: 专家提醒，家庭暴力不是私事，不能拿{家丑不可外扬}当借口。
ctx.en: Experts warn that domestic violence is not a private matter, and keeping family shame hidden is no excuse.

bad.s: 我考了第一名，{家丑不可外扬}，先别告诉别人。
bad.en: (meant: I came first in the exam, but don't tell anyone yet)
bad.why: The saying is about something shameful in the family; good news is not shameful, so there is nothing to hide.

bad.s: 他把公司的核心技术卖给了对手，真是{家丑不可外扬}。
bad.en: (meant: he sold the company's key technology to a rival)
bad.why: The saying tells people to keep embarrassing matters inside; it does not describe leaking secrets, which are not shameful affairs.

cards.r: huò bǐ sān jiā bù chī kuī
cards.mean: compare several sellers before you buy
cards.lit: compare the goods at three shops and you won't lose out

use.how: Said as advice before a purchase, or to explain why one is shopping around: 别急着买，货比三家不吃亏。 三 just means several.

near.diff: 一分钱一分货 says that a higher price buys better quality; 货比三家不吃亏 says to compare several sellers before deciding.

cards.cue: Your friend is about to buy the first laptop she sees in the first shop. You suggest checking a few other stores first. What saying backs you up?

ctx.s: 先别买，再去别的店看看，{货比三家不吃亏}。
ctx.en: Don't buy it yet; let's look in other shops. It pays to shop around.

ctx.s: 买手机我一般会在网上多看几家，{货比三家不吃亏}嘛。
ctx.en: When I buy a phone I usually check a few sellers online. Comparing never hurts.

ctx.s: “这家的价格已经不错了吧？”“{货比三家不吃亏}，明天再问问别家。”
ctx.en: "This shop's price is pretty good already, isn't it?" "It pays to compare. Let's ask a few others tomorrow."

ctx.s: 装修房子前，他跑了五家建材市场，说{货比三家不吃亏}。
ctx.en: Before renovating his flat he went round five building-supply markets, saying you never lose by shopping around.

ctx.s: 公司采购办公用品也讲究{货比三家不吃亏}，至少要拿到三份报价。
ctx.en: Even when the company buys office supplies it follows the rule of shopping around: at least three quotes are required.

ctx.s: 妈妈买菜从来不在第一个摊位停下，她的口头禅就是{货比三家不吃亏}。
ctx.en: Mum never stops at the first stall when she buys vegetables; her motto is that it pays to compare.

bad.s: 他只吃这家店的面，{货比三家不吃亏}。
bad.en: (meant: he only eats the noodles at this one shop)
bad.why: The saying urges comparing several sellers, so it cannot back up sticking loyally to one.

bad.s: 我们班这三个同学，{货比三家不吃亏}，看看谁成绩最好。
bad.en: (meant: let's compare these three classmates and see whose grades are best)
bad.why: It is about shopping: comparing goods and prices before buying, not comparing people.

cards.r: yǒu qián néng shǐ guǐ tuī mò
cards.mean: with enough money you can get anyone to do anything
cards.lit: if you have money, you can even make a ghost turn the millstone

use.how: Said cynically or wryly about money getting done what otherwise would not be done, often after 真是 or 以为: 真是有钱能使鬼推磨。

cards.cue: A restaurant that told everyone it was fully booked suddenly finds a table when a rich man slips the manager a thick envelope. What do the people waiting mutter?

ctx.s: 一加钱，师傅马上就来修了，真是{有钱能使鬼推磨}。
ctx.en: As soon as we offered more money, the repairman came right over. Money really does talk.

ctx.s: 刚才还说没房间，给了小费就有了，{有钱能使鬼推磨}啊！
ctx.en: A minute ago they had no rooms, and after a tip there's one. Money can buy anything!

ctx.s: 他总以为{有钱能使鬼推磨}，结果这次花再多钱也没用。
ctx.en: He always thought money could make anyone do anything, but this time no amount of money helped.

ctx.s: “他的手续怎么这么快就办好了？”“你说呢？{有钱能使鬼推磨}呗。”
ctx.en: "How did his paperwork get done so fast?" "What do you think? Money gets things moving."

ctx.s: 小说里的老板相信{有钱能使鬼推磨}，可到最后连家人都离开了他。
ctx.en: The boss in the novel believes money can buy anything, yet in the end even his family leaves him.

ctx.s: 有人说{有钱能使鬼推磨}，但真正的朋友是用钱买不来的。
ctx.en: Some say money can make anyone do anything, but true friends can't be bought.

bad.s: 他努力赚钱养家，真是{有钱能使鬼推磨}。
bad.en: (meant: he works hard to earn money for his family)
bad.why: The saying is a cynical remark about money making others do one's bidding; it is not praise for earning a living.

bad.s: 这个月工资涨了，{有钱能使鬼推磨}，我好开心。
bad.en: (meant: I got a pay rise this month and I'm so happy)
bad.why: It is not about the joy of having money but about money buying other people's help or cooperation.

cards.t: 人往高处走，水往低处流
cards.r: rén wǎng gāo chù zǒu, shuǐ wǎng dī chù liú
cards.mean: it's only natural for people to seek a better position
cards.lit: people walk toward higher places, water flows toward lower ones

use.how: Said to explain or accept someone leaving for a better job, school or city, usually with understanding rather than blame: 人往高处走，水往低处流，他跳槽很正常。

cards.cue: Your best employee tells you she has an offer from a bigger firm at double the pay. You don't hold it against her. What do you say?

ctx.s: 他去了更好的公司，{人往高处走，水往低处流}嘛。
ctx.en: He moved to a better company. Everyone wants to get ahead, after all.

ctx.s: 女儿想去大城市发展，妈妈虽然不舍，也知道{人往高处走，水往低处流}。
ctx.en: The daughter wants to build her career in a big city; her mother hates to let her go, but knows it's natural to aim higher.

ctx.s: “小李要辞职了，你不生气吗？”“{人往高处走，水往低处流}，我祝福他。”
ctx.en: "Xiao Li is quitting. Aren't you angry?" "People naturally go where things are better. I wish him well."

ctx.s: 村里的年轻人都去城里打工了，老人们说，{人往高处走，水往低处流}，留不住的。
ctx.en: The young people have all gone to work in the cities; the old folk say it's only natural to seek a better life, and you can't keep them.

ctx.s: {人往高处走，水往低处流}，想换个更好的平台，这没什么丢人的。
ctx.en: It's natural to want to move up; wanting a better platform is nothing to be ashamed of.

ctx.s: 老板明白{人往高处走，水往低处流}，所以用加薪和培训来留住人才。
ctx.en: The boss understands that people will always look for something better, so he keeps talent with raises and training.

bad.s: 他被公司降职了，真是{人往高处走，水往低处流}。
bad.en: (meant: he was demoted)
bad.why: It explains people moving up to something better, not someone dropping to a lower position.

bad.s: 我们周末去爬山吧，{人往高处走，水往低处流}。
bad.en: (meant: let's go hiking at the weekend)
bad.why: The higher place is a better job or life, not a literal mountain.

cards.r: xīn guān shàng rèn sān bǎ huǒ
cards.mean: a new boss always starts with a burst of vigorous changes
cards.lit: a new official, on taking office, lights three fires

use.how: Said, often wryly, about a newly appointed leader making a flurry of changes or tough rules at the start: 新官上任三把火，你看他这几天忙的。

near.diff: 一朝天子一朝臣 says a new leader brings in their own people; 新官上任三把火 says a new leader opens with a burst of reforms and strictness.

cards.cue: Your department gets a new director, and in her first week she bans phones in meetings, changes the schedule and starts spot checks. How do colleagues sum it up?

ctx.s: 新校长一来就改了作息时间，{新官上任三把火}嘛。
ctx.en: The new principal changed the timetable the moment she arrived. A new broom sweeps clean.

ctx.s: “新主任要求每天八点开会。”“{新官上任三把火}，过一阵就好了。”
ctx.en: "The new director wants a meeting at eight every day." "New bosses always start out fired up. It'll settle down."

ctx.s: 他刚当上队长就定了一堆新规矩，大家笑他{新官上任三把火}。
ctx.en: He'd barely become captain before he laid down a pile of new rules, and everyone teased him about the new-boss zeal.

ctx.s: 都说{新官上任三把火}，可新经理来了一个月，什么都没改。
ctx.en: They say a new boss always shakes things up, but the new manager has been here a month and hasn't changed a thing.

ctx.s: 新市长一上任就连推三项改革，真应了那句{新官上任三把火}。
ctx.en: The new mayor launched three reforms in a row right after taking office, just as the saying about new officials goes.

ctx.s: 我刚当上组长，不想搞{新官上任三把火}那一套，打算先听听大家的意见。
ctx.en: I've just become team leader, and I don't want to do the new-boss shake-up thing; I plan to hear everyone out first.

bad.s: 他刚来公司当实习生，{新官上任三把火}，特别努力。
bad.en: (meant: he's a new intern and works really hard)
bad.why: It is about a new boss or official imposing changes, not a low-ranking newcomer working hard.

bad.s: 新经理今天发了很大的脾气，{新官上任三把火}。
bad.en: (meant: the new manager lost his temper badly today)
bad.why: The fires are reforms and tough measures at the start of a term, not a fit of anger.

cards.r: sān gè hé shang méi shuǐ chī
cards.mean: when a job belongs to everyone, nobody ends up doing it
cards.lit: three monks, and no water to drink

story.text: The saying is the last line of a three-step folk rhyme: one monk carries his own water, two monks carry it together, three monks have no water to drink. Alone, a monk fetches water himself with two buckets on a shoulder pole; two monks carry one bucket slung between them; with three, each waits for the others to go, and nobody fetches any. The rhyme became widely known through the 1980 Shanghai Animation Film Studio cartoon Three Monks.
story.source: folk rhyme 一个和尚挑水吃，两个和尚抬水吃，三个和尚没水吃; animated film 《三个和尚》 (1980)

use.how: Said about a group in which shared responsibility means nobody acts; sometimes the fuller rhyme is quoted. 人多了，反而三个和尚没水吃。

near.diff: 众人拾柴火焰高 praises many people all contributing; 三个和尚没水吃 criticises many people each leaving the job to someone else.

cards.cue: Four flatmates share a kitchen; each assumes someone else will take out the rubbish, and it piles up for two weeks. What sums it up?

ctx.s: 宿舍的垃圾一个星期没人倒，真是{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: Nobody in the dorm has taken out the rubbish for a week. Everybody's job is nobody's job.

ctx.s: 这件事最好指定一个负责人，不然{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: We'd better put one person in charge of this, or with everyone responsible, nothing will get done.

ctx.s: “办公室的饮水机谁去换水？”“谁都不去，{三个和尚没水吃}呗。”
ctx.en: "Who's going to change the office water cooler?" "Nobody. Everyone leaves it to everyone else."

ctx.s: 项目组加了人，进度反而更慢了，大家互相推，成了{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: The project team got more people, but progress actually slowed; everyone passed the buck and nothing got done.

ctx.s: 小区的路灯坏了半年，物业和居委会都说不归自己管，{三个和尚没水吃}。
ctx.en: The streetlight in our estate has been broken for six months; the management company and the residents' committee both say it's not their job, so nobody fixes it.

ctx.s: 管理学课上，老师用{三个和尚没水吃}的例子说明责任必须分清。
ctx.en: In management class, the teacher used the three-monks story to show that responsibilities must be clearly assigned.

bad.s: 我们三个人一起努力，{三个和尚没水吃}，很快就完成了。
bad.en: (meant: the three of us worked together and finished quickly)
bad.why: It describes a group where nobody does the job, the opposite of successful teamwork.

bad.s: 家里停水了，{三个和尚没水吃}。
bad.en: (meant: the water supply at home has been cut off)
bad.why: It is not about actually lacking water but about people shirking a shared duty.

cards.r: zhòng rén shí chái huǒ yàn gāo
cards.mean: when everyone pitches in, together they achieve far more
cards.lit: when everyone gathers firewood, the flames burn high

use.how: Said to call for or praise joint effort, often in team pep talks, appeals and donation drives: 大家一起出力，众人拾柴火焰高。

near.t: 三个臭皮匠，顶个诸葛亮
near.diff: 三个臭皮匠，顶个诸葛亮 is about pooling ideas to solve a problem; 众人拾柴火焰高 is about everyone contributing effort or resources.
三个和尚没水吃 is the failure case, where a crowd shirks the job; 众人拾柴火焰高 is the success case, where everyone contributes.

cards.cue: A classmate's family can't afford an operation, so everyone at school gives a little, and together it covers the whole cost. What saying fits?

ctx.s: 大家都出一点力，{众人拾柴火焰高}嘛。
ctx.en: Let's all do our bit. Many hands make light work.

ctx.s: 一个人搬不完，叫上邻居一起，{众人拾柴火焰高}，半天就搬好了。
ctx.en: One person couldn't have moved it all, but with the neighbours pitching in, it was done in half a day.

ctx.s: “这么多活儿，我们几个干得完吗？”“放心，{众人拾柴火焰高}。”
ctx.en: "Can just a few of us get all this work done?" "Don't worry. If we all pitch in, we will."

ctx.s: 全村每家捐一点，{众人拾柴火焰高}，终于修好了那座桥。
ctx.en: Every household in the village gave a little, and together they finally got the bridge repaired.

ctx.s: 倡议书最后写道：{众人拾柴火焰高}，期待每一位居民的参与。
ctx.en: The appeal ended: when everyone contributes, we achieve far more; we hope every resident will take part.

ctx.s: 球队没有明星球员，靠的是团结，正所谓{众人拾柴火焰高}。
ctx.en: The team had no star players; it relied on unity. As they say, when everyone adds fuel, the fire burns high.

bad.s: 他一个人熬夜完成了全部工作，真是{众人拾柴火焰高}。
bad.en: (meant: he stayed up all night and finished all the work by himself)
bad.why: It credits many people contributing together, not one person working alone.

bad.s: 地铁里人太多了，挤得要命，{众人拾柴火焰高}。
bad.en: (meant: the subway is packed and terribly crowded)
bad.why: It praises joint effort toward a goal, not a mere crowd of people.

cards.t: 台上一分钟，台下十年功
cards.r: tái shàng yī fēn zhōng, tái xià shí nián gōng
cards.mean: a brief moment of brilliance rests on years of practice
cards.lit: one minute on the stage, ten years of training off it

use.how: Said in admiration of a performance, match or skill that looks effortless, pointing to the long practice behind it: 他弹得这么好，真是台上一分钟，台下十年功。

near.t: 只要功夫深，铁杵磨成针
near.diff: 铁杵磨成针 encourages someone to persevere at a hard task; 台上一分钟，台下十年功 explains a polished performance by the years of practice behind it.

cards.cue: After a gymnast's flawless ninety-second routine, the commentator reminds viewers that she has trained daily since she was five. What saying does he use?

ctx.s: 她跳得这么好，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}啊。
