ctx.en: She dances so beautifully. Behind every minute on stage are years of practice.

ctx.s: 别看魔术师变得那么轻松，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}。
ctx.en: The magician makes it look so easy, but that ease takes years of practice.

ctx.s: “他演讲怎么一点都不紧张？”“{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，他私下练了很多遍。”
ctx.en: "How come he's not nervous at all when he speaks?" "It looks easy because he's practised it over and over in private."

ctx.s: 京剧老师常对学生说：“{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，基本功一天也不能停。”
ctx.en: The Peking opera teacher often tells students: "Every minute on stage rests on ten years of work behind the scenes; never skip a day of basic training."

ctx.s: 冠军那套动作只有两分钟，正所谓{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，她从五岁就开始练了。
ctx.en: The champion's routine lasted only two minutes, but as they say, a moment of brilliance takes years of work: she started training at five.

ctx.s: 很多人只看到明星的风光，却不明白{台上一分钟，台下十年功}的道理。
ctx.en: Many people only see a star's glamour and don't understand that it rests on years of hard work.

bad.s: 这次考试我没复习，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}，结果考砸了。
bad.en: (meant: I didn't revise for the exam and failed)
bad.why: It praises the long practice behind a fine performance; it cannot describe a failure caused by no preparation.

bad.s: 电影太长了，{台上一分钟，台下十年功}。
bad.en: (meant: the film felt endlessly long)
bad.why: The numbers contrast a short performance with long training; they say nothing about time dragging.

cards.t: 吃得苦中苦，方为人上人
cards.r: chī de kǔ zhōng kǔ, fāng wéi rén shàng rén
cards.mean: only by enduring great hardship can you rise above others
cards.lit: only one who can eat the bitterest of bitterness becomes a person above others

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, often by parents, elders or coaches, to urge someone to put up with hardship now for a better future: 坚持住，吃得苦中苦，方为人上人。

near.t: 台上一分钟，台下十年功
near.diff: 台上一分钟 explains that a brief brilliant moment rests on years of practice; 吃得苦中苦 urges someone to endure hardship to get ahead in life.

cards.cue: Your teenage cousin moans that the endless hours of exam preparation are unbearable. Their grandmother wants them to grit their teeth so they can make something of themselves. What does she say?

ctx.s: 别喊累了，{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}。
ctx.en: Stop complaining that you're tired. Only those who endure real hardship get ahead.

ctx.s: 小时候爷爷总对我说：“{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}。”
ctx.en: When I was little, Grandpa always told me: "Only by enduring the worst hardship can you rise above others."

ctx.s: 训练再苦也得坚持，想出人头地，就得记住{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}。
ctx.en: However hard the training, you have to stick with it; if you want to get ahead, remember that only those who endure hardship rise above others.

ctx.s: 你觉得{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}这句话现在还有道理吗？
ctx.en: Do you think the saying that only those who endure hardship rise above others still makes sense today?

ctx.s: 他在工地上干了好几年，常说{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}，现在自己开了公司。
ctx.en: He worked on building sites for years, always saying you have to endure hardship to get ahead; now he runs his own company.

ctx.s: 当年家里穷，父母相信{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}，咬着牙供我们读完了大学。
ctx.en: Our family was poor back then; my parents believed hardship endured leads to a better life, and gritted their teeth to put us through university.

bad.s: 他天天睡到中午，真是{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}。
bad.en: (meant: he sleeps till noon every day, what a lazy man)
bad.why: It praises enduring hardship in order to get ahead, so it cannot describe or mock someone who is lazy.

bad.s: 他生病住院了，{吃得苦中苦，方为人上人}。
bad.en: (meant: he's in hospital, I hope he gets better)
bad.why: It is about choosing to endure hardship in order to rise in life, not a comfort for illness or bad luck.

cards.t: 少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲
cards.r: shào zhuàng bù nǔ lì, lǎo dà tú shāng bēi
cards.mean: idle in your youth and you will regret it when you are old
cards.lit: if you do not strive while young and strong, when old you will grieve in vain

story.text: The line closes a Han-dynasty folk song, 'A Long Song'. It begins with green mallows in a garden waiting for the morning sun to dry their dew; spring brings everything to life, but the singer fears autumn, when the leaves turn yellow and wither. A hundred rivers flow east to the sea; when will they ever flow back west? So, the song ends, if you do not work hard while young and strong, in old age you will grieve in vain.

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, usually by elders to the young, to warn them not to waste their youth; also quoted ruefully by older people about themselves.

near.diff: 一寸光阴一寸金 says all time is precious; 少壮不努力 warns specifically that a wasted youth brings regret in old age.
书到用时方恨少 is the regret felt at one moment of need; 少壮不努力 looks across a whole life, from youth to old age.

cards.cue: A father watches his sixteen-year-old play games all night instead of studying, and warns him that throwing away these years will haunt him decades from now. What saying does he use?

ctx.s: 趁年轻多学点东西吧，别等老了再后悔，{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}啊。
ctx.en: Learn all you can while you're young; don't wait to regret it when you're old. Slack off now and you'll grieve for it later.

ctx.s: 老师在黑板上写下{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}，让我们抄在本子上。
ctx.en: The teacher wrote "idle in youth, grieve in old age" on the board and had us copy it into our notebooks.

ctx.s: 你天天打游戏，不怕{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}吗？
ctx.en: You play games all day. Aren't you afraid you'll waste your youth and regret it when you're old?

ctx.s: 爷爷叹了口气：“我年轻时不爱读书，现在才懂什么叫{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}。”
ctx.en: Grandpa sighed: "I didn't like studying when I was young; only now do I understand what it means to grieve in old age for an idle youth."

ctx.s: 他把{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}贴在书桌前，怕自己年纪大了才后悔。
ctx.en: He stuck "idle in youth, grieve in old age" above his desk, afraid that otherwise he would regret it when he was older.

ctx.s: 人到中年才发现，{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}这句老话一点也不假。
ctx.en: Only in middle age do you find that the old saying about an idle youth and a regretful old age is perfectly true.

bad.s: 他退休以后天天锻炼，真是{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}。
bad.en: (meant: since retiring he exercises every day, good for him)
bad.why: It is a warning about regret for a wasted youth, not praise for staying active in old age.

bad.s: 爷爷，您快去学电脑吧，{少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲}。
bad.en: (meant: Grandpa, go and learn to use a computer, it's never too late)
bad.why: It is said to the young about using their youth; urging an old person to start learning calls for a different saying.

cards.r: shū dào yòng shí fāng hèn shǎo
cards.mean: only when you need knowledge do you regret not studying more
cards.lit: only when the time comes to use books do you regret having read too few

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, usually about oneself, at a moment when one's knowledge falls short: 写论文时才知道书到用时方恨少。 Also used to urge others to read more.

near.t: 少壮不努力，老大徒伤悲
near.diff: 少壮不努力 warns of regret in old age for a whole wasted youth; 书到用时方恨少 is the regret felt at one particular moment of need.

cards.cue: A foreign visitor asks you to explain a famous painting in a museum, and you realise you know almost nothing about art history and wish you had read up on it. What do you sigh?

ctx.s: 想写封像样的信，却一句也写不出来，真是{书到用时方恨少}。
ctx.en: I wanted to write a decent letter but couldn't come up with a single line. You only regret not reading more when you need it.

ctx.s: 客户问了几个专业问题，我一个都答不上，这才明白{书到用时方恨少}。
ctx.en: The client asked a few technical questions and I couldn't answer one of them; only then did I see how true it is that you regret not studying more when you need it.

ctx.s: 带孩子逛博物馆，孩子问个不停，我只能感叹{书到用时方恨少}。
ctx.en: Taking my child round the museum, I got question after question, and all I could do was sigh that I hadn't read more.

ctx.s: “你怎么突然开始看历史书了？”“{书到用时方恨少}嘛，下个月要当导游。”
ctx.en: "Why have you suddenly started reading history books?" "You only find out how little you know when you need it. I'm guiding tours next month."

ctx.s: 第一次去国外开会，我才体会到{书到用时方恨少}，很多词都不会说。
ctx.en: At my first conference abroad I learned how true it is that you regret not studying more only when you need it; there were so many words I couldn't say.

ctx.s: 平时多读点书吧，别等到{书到用时方恨少}的时候再着急。
ctx.en: Read more in everyday life; don't wait until the knowledge you lack is suddenly needed and then panic.

bad.s: 我买了太多书，书架都放不下了，真是{书到用时方恨少}。
bad.en: (meant: I've bought so many books my shelves can't hold them)
bad.why: It is about regretting how little one has read when knowledge is needed, not about owning too many books.

bad.s: 这家书店的书太少了，{书到用时方恨少}。
bad.en: (meant: this bookshop doesn't stock enough books)
bad.why: The shortfall is in one's own reading and knowledge, not a shortage of books for sale.

cards.r: dú wàn juàn shū, xíng wàn lǐ lù
cards.mean: learn both from reading widely and from travelling far
cards.lit: read ten thousand scrolls of books, travel ten thousand li of road

use.how: Quoted as a whole sentence, or as the object of verbs like 做到, 讲, 提倡, for the ideal of learning both from books and from travel.

near.diff: 百闻不如一见 says seeing one thing for yourself beats hearsay; 读万卷书，行万里路 is a lifelong ideal joining broad reading with wide travel.

cards.cue: A school runs a programme in which students spend a term on intensive reading and then go on study trips around the country. Which saying sums up its two-part aim?

ctx.s: {读万卷书，行万里路}，光看书不出门可不行。
ctx.en: Read widely and travel far: reading books without ever leaving home won't do.

ctx.s: 退休以后，他终于有时间{读万卷书，行万里路}了。
ctx.en: After retiring, he finally had time to read widely and travel far.

ctx.s: 这次研学旅行让孩子们明白了什么叫{读万卷书，行万里路}。
ctx.en: This study trip showed the children what it means to learn both from books and from the road.

ctx.s: 你觉得{读万卷书，行万里路}，哪一个更重要？
ctx.en: Reading widely or travelling far: which do you think matters more?

ctx.s: 她背着书走遍了大半个中国，真正做到了{读万卷书，行万里路}。
ctx.en: With books in her backpack she travelled across most of China, truly learning from both reading and the road.

ctx.s: 古人讲{读万卷书，行万里路}，今天的年轻人出国留学也是这个道理。
ctx.en: The ancients spoke of reading ten thousand books and travelling ten thousand li; young people who study abroad today follow the same idea.

bad.s: 他每天跑步十公里，真是{读万卷书，行万里路}。
bad.en: (meant: he runs ten kilometres every day)
bad.why: Its second half means travelling to see the world and learn from it, not physical exercise or distance covered.

bad.s: 这本书太长了，我得{读万卷书，行万里路}才能看完。
bad.en: (meant: this book is so long it will take me forever to finish)
bad.why: It is an ideal of broad learning from books and travel, not an exaggeration of how long one task takes.

cards.r: sān rén xíng, bì yǒu wǒ shī
cards.mean: there is something to learn from anyone around you
cards.lit: when three people walk together, one of them is sure to be my teacher

story.text: In the Analects, Confucius says that whenever three people walk together, there is sure to be a teacher for him among them: he picks out their good points and follows them, and where he sees their faults, he corrects the same faults in himself. The line is quoted to this day to praise humility and the habit of learning from anyone.

use.how: Quoted as a whole sentence to say one should humbly learn from the people around, even those younger or junior: 三人行，必有我师，向同事学习不丢人。

near.diff: 活到老，学到老 is about never stopping learning throughout life; 三人行，必有我师 is about learning from the people around you.

cards.cue: A senior engineer gladly takes tips on a new tool from a junior intern and tells the team that a teacher can turn up in anyone. Which line from Confucius does he quote?

ctx.s: {三人行，必有我师}，多听听别人的意见没坏处。
ctx.en: There's a teacher in any company; it does no harm to listen to other people's views.

ctx.s: 老教授常向学生请教，他说{三人行，必有我师}。
ctx.en: The old professor often asks his students for advice; there's always someone to learn from, he says.

ctx.s: 新来的实习生电脑用得很熟，经理笑着说：“{三人行，必有我师}，我得跟你学学。”
ctx.en: The new intern was great with computers. The manager laughed: "There's always someone to learn from. I'd better take lessons from you."

ctx.s: 孔子都说{三人行，必有我师}，你怎么能看不起别人呢？
ctx.en: Even Confucius said there is a teacher among any three people. How can you look down on others?

ctx.s: 在农村住了一个月，我发现{三人行，必有我师}，农民懂的东西比我多多了。
ctx.en: After a month in the countryside I found there really is a teacher in everyone; the farmers knew far more than I did.

ctx.s: {三人行，必有我师}，同事身上的优点，我都记在本子上。
ctx.en: Everyone has something to teach; I write down my colleagues' strengths in a notebook.

bad.s: 我们三个人一起去旅行，{三人行，必有我师}。
bad.en: (meant: the three of us went on a trip together)
bad.why: The three people are not a literal count of travel companions; the saying is about learning humbly from others.

bad.s: 学校给我们班请了一位很好的数学老师，{三人行，必有我师}。
bad.en: (meant: the school hired a very good maths teacher for our class)
bad.why: It means anyone around you can teach you something, not that a class has been given a teacher.

cards.r: shān wài yǒu shān, rén wài yǒu rén
cards.mean: there is always someone better than you, so stay modest
cards.lit: beyond the mountain there are more mountains; beyond the person there are more people

use.how: Said as a whole sentence to warn someone, or oneself, against arrogance, or after meeting someone far more skilled: 别骄傲，山外有山，人外有人。

near.diff: 三人行 says you can learn from anyone around you; 山外有山，人外有人 says someone is always better than you, so do not be proud.

cards.cue: Your nephew wins his school chess tournament and starts boasting that nobody can beat him. Before his first national competition, what do you remind him?

ctx.s: 别太得意了，{山外有山，人外有人}。
ctx.en: Don't get too full of yourself; there's always someone better.

ctx.s: {山外有山，人外有人}，咱们还得接着练。
ctx.en: There's always someone stronger out there, so we need to keep training.

ctx.s: 他以为自己是全校跑得最快的，到了省里比赛才知道{山外有山，人外有人}。
ctx.en: He thought he was the fastest runner in his school; only at the provincial meet did he learn there's always someone faster.

ctx.s: “这次冠军肯定是我的。”“话别说太满，{山外有山，人外有人}。”
ctx.en: "I'm sure to win this time." "Don't speak too soon. There's always someone better."

ctx.s: 见识了老师傅的手艺，他终于明白{山外有山，人外有人}，再也不吹牛了。
ctx.en: Once he had seen the old master's craftsmanship, he finally understood there is always someone better, and stopped bragging.

ctx.s: 公司里个个都是高手，刚来时我才体会到什么叫{山外有山，人外有人}。
ctx.en: Everyone at the company is an expert; when I first arrived I really felt what it means that there's always someone better.

bad.s: 我家后面{山外有山，人外有人}，风景很美。
bad.en: (meant: there are mountains behind my house and the scenery is lovely)
bad.why: It is not a description of scenery; it is a warning that there is always someone better than you.

bad.s: 他是全世界最厉害的，{山外有山，人外有人}。
bad.en: (meant: he is the best in the whole world)
bad.why: It denies that anyone is unbeatable, so it cannot back up a claim that someone is the very best.

cards.r: qīng chū yú lán ér shèng yú lán
cards.mean: the student comes to surpass the teacher
cards.lit: blue dye comes from the indigo plant, yet it is bluer than the indigo

story.text: Xunzi opens his essay 'Encouraging Learning' by saying that learning must never stop. Blue dye, he writes, is taken from the indigo plant, yet it is bluer than the indigo; ice is made from water, yet it is colder than water. Later readers took the first image to mean that a student, through learning, can come to surpass the teacher.

use.how: Used as a predicate or quoted whole, to praise a student or junior who has outdone their own teacher or elder; often shortened to 青出于蓝.

near.diff: 后浪推前浪 is about whole generations overtaking each other; 青出于蓝 praises a particular student who surpasses their own teacher.

cards.cue: A piano teacher sits in the audience as her former pupil wins an international prize she herself never won, and glows with pride. What saying fits the moment?

ctx.s: 徒弟的手艺已经超过了师傅，真是{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}。
ctx.en: The apprentice's craft has now outstripped his master's: the student has truly surpassed the teacher.

ctx.s: 看到学生拿了大奖，老教练笑着说：“{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}，我高兴啊！”
ctx.en: Seeing his pupil win a big prize, the old coach smiled: "The student has outdone the teacher. I couldn't be happier!"

ctx.s: 王老师最大的心愿，就是学生们能{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}。
ctx.en: Ms Wang's dearest wish is that her students will one day surpass her.

ctx.s: 评论家都说这位年轻画家{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}，画得比他的老师更有灵气。
ctx.en: Critics all say this young painter has outdone his teacher; his work has more spark than his teacher's.

ctx.s: 女儿跟着妈妈学书法，现在写得比妈妈还好，大家都夸她{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}。
ctx.en: The daughter learned calligraphy from her mother and now writes better than her; everyone praises her for surpassing her teacher.

ctx.s: 学生超过老师，是老师的失败吗？我看{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}，正是老师的骄傲。
ctx.en: Is it the teacher's failure when a student does better? I'd say a student outdoing the teacher is the teacher's pride.

bad.s: 学了三年，他还是不如老师，真是{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}。
bad.en: (meant: after three years he is still not as good as his teacher)
bad.why: It says the student has become better than the teacher, the opposite of still falling short.

bad.s: 这件衣服比那件还蓝，{青出于蓝而胜于蓝}。
bad.en: (meant: this shirt is an even deeper blue than that one)
bad.why: The colours are only the image; it is said of a student surpassing a teacher, not of comparing shades of blue.

cards.r: cháng jiāng hòu làng tuī qián làng
cards.mean: each new generation overtakes the one that came before
cards.lit: on the Yangtze the waves behind push on the waves ahead

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, often by older people half in admiration and half in self-mockery, about young newcomers overtaking the established: 真是长江后浪推前浪。

near.diff: 青出于蓝 praises one student who surpasses their own teacher; 长江后浪推前浪 is about newcomers in general overtaking the older generation.

cards.cue: A veteran table-tennis champion loses the final to a teenager nobody had heard of, and at the press conference jokes good-naturedly about his age. What saying fits?

ctx.s: 现在的年轻人真厉害，{长江后浪推前浪}啊。
ctx.en: Young people today are amazing. Each new generation really does push past the last.

ctx.s: 老冠军输给了十七岁的新人，赛后他笑着说：“{长江后浪推前浪}嘛。”
ctx.en: The veteran champion lost to a seventeen-year-old newcomer; afterwards he laughed: "Well, the new waves always push the old ones along."

ctx.s: {长江后浪推前浪}，这几年手机行业冒出了很多新公司。
ctx.en: The new keep overtaking the old: lots of new companies have sprung up in the phone industry in recent years.

ctx.s: 我们这些老员工得多学习，不然{长江后浪推前浪}，很快就被比下去了。
ctx.en: We old hands need to keep learning, or the younger generation will soon overtake us.

ctx.s: 看着台上的新一代歌手，老歌迷感叹：“真是{长江后浪推前浪}。”
ctx.en: Watching the new generation of singers on stage, the long-time fans sighed: "Each wave really does push on the one before."

ctx.s: 文坛{长江后浪推前浪}，一批年轻作家正在崛起。
ctx.en: In the literary world each generation overtakes the last; a group of young writers is now on the rise.

bad.s: 今天江上风很大，{长江后浪推前浪}，船都不敢开了。
bad.en: (meant: it's very windy on the river today, and the boats daren't sail)
bad.why: The waves are only an image; it is a saying about generations, not a report on actual waves.

bad.s: 这家老字号一百年来一直是第一，真是{长江后浪推前浪}。
bad.en: (meant: this old brand has been number one for a century)
bad.why: It says newcomers overtake the old, so it cannot praise an old firm that has stayed on top.

cards.r: bīng dòng sān chǐ, fēi yī rì zhī hán
cards.mean: a deep-rooted problem has been building up for a long time
cards.lit: ice three feet thick is not the work of a single day's cold

use.how: Said as a whole sentence to explain that a serious problem, conflict or bad habit took a long time to form, and so will not be fixed quickly.

near.diff: 一口吃不成胖子 says good results must be built step by step; 冰冻三尺 explains that a serious problem took a long time to develop.

cards.cue: A couple who seemed fine suddenly announce their divorce, but close friends know resentment had been piling up between them for years. How do the friends explain it?

ctx.s: 他们俩的矛盾不是一天两天了，{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}。
ctx.en: Their quarrel didn't start yesterday; trouble this deep has been building for a long time.

ctx.s: 这家公司怎么突然倒闭了？其实{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}，问题早就有了。
ctx.en: How did the company suddenly go bust? Actually it had been coming for ages; the problems were there all along.

ctx.s: 医生说他的胃病是长期不吃早饭落下的，{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}。
ctx.en: The doctor said his stomach trouble came from years of skipping breakfast; it didn't happen overnight.

ctx.s: “他怎么突然辞职了？”“{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}，他对老板不满很久了。”
ctx.en: "Why did he suddenly quit?" "It's been building up for ages. He's been unhappy with the boss for a long time."

ctx.s: 孩子厌学，{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}，家长也该想想自己的原因。
ctx.en: A child's hatred of school builds up over a long time; parents should also think about their own part in it.

ctx.s: 城市的交通问题是几十年积累下来的，{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}。
ctx.en: The city's traffic problems have built up over decades; trouble this deep doesn't form in a day.

bad.s: 今天突然降温了，{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}。
bad.en: (meant: the temperature suddenly dropped today)
bad.why: The ice and cold are only the image; it explains that a deep problem built up over time, not today's weather.

bad.s: 他们昨天才认识，今天就吵起来了，{冰冻三尺，非一日之寒}。
bad.en: (meant: they only met yesterday and are already quarrelling)
bad.why: It explains trouble that built up over a long time, so it contradicts a quarrel that came out of nowhere.

cards.r: jī bù kě shī, shí bù zài lái
cards.mean: act now: a chance like this will not come again
cards.lit: the opportunity must not be lost; its moment will not come again

use.how: Said as a whole sentence to urge someone, or oneself, to seize a chance at once: 机不可失，时不再来，你赶紧报名吧。 Also common in advertising and sales talk.

near.diff: 一寸光阴一寸金 says all time is precious; 机不可失，时不再来 is about one particular chance that will soon be gone.

cards.cue: Your friend is hesitating over a rare scholarship whose applications close tomorrow and which may never be offered again. What do you tell them?

ctx.s: {机不可失，时不再来}，你快去报名吧！
ctx.en: Don't let this chance slip; it won't come again. Go and sign up!

ctx.s: 这么好的工作机会，{机不可失，时不再来}，你还犹豫什么？
ctx.en: A job offer this good won't come round twice. What are you hesitating for?

ctx.s: 商场门口写着：“全场五折，仅限今天，{机不可失，时不再来}！”
ctx.en: The sign at the mall entrance read: "Everything half price, today only. Don't miss out, it won't come again!"

ctx.s: 他知道{机不可失，时不再来}，当天就买了去北京的车票。
ctx.en: He knew a chance like this would not come again, and bought a ticket to Beijing that same day.

ctx.s: 教练对队员们喊：“对方已经累了，{机不可失，时不再来}，马上进攻！”
ctx.en: The coach shouted to the players: "They're worn out. This chance won't come again. Attack now!"

ctx.s: 很多人想等房价再降一点，也有人觉得{机不可失，时不再来}，赶紧买了。
ctx.en: Many people want to wait for house prices to fall further, but some felt it was now or never and bought straight away.

bad.s: 别着急，慢慢等，{机不可失，时不再来}。
bad.en: (meant: no hurry, just wait patiently)
bad.why: It urges acting at once before a chance disappears, so it cannot go with advice to wait.

bad.s: 我的手机丢了，{机不可失，时不再来}。
bad.en: (meant: I've lost my phone)
bad.why: The ji in the saying means an opportunity, not a phone or other machine; it urges seizing a chance, not regret over a lost object.

cards.t: 天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福
cards.r: tiān yǒu bù cè fēng yún, rén yǒu dàn xī huò fú
cards.mean: disaster can strike anyone suddenly and without warning
cards.lit: the sky has wind and clouds no one can predict; people have fortune and disaster between morning and night

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, often with a sigh, after someone suffers a sudden accident, illness or loss, or to argue for being prepared: 真是天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福。

near.diff: 屋漏偏逢连夜雨 is one misfortune piling onto another; 天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福 says a misfortune can strike out of the blue.

cards.cue: A fit, healthy neighbour in his forties was rushed to hospital last night with a stroke. Everyone in the building sighs that nobody could have seen it coming.

ctx.s: 谁也想不到他会突然生病，真是{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}。
ctx.en: Nobody imagined he would suddenly fall ill. You really never know what's coming.

ctx.s: 昨天还好好的，今天就出了车祸，唉，{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}啊。
ctx.en: He was perfectly fine yesterday, and today he's had a car accident. Sigh, disaster can strike anyone at any time.

ctx.s: {天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，买份保险总是有备无患。
ctx.en: Misfortune can come without warning, so taking out insurance is always a sensible precaution.

ctx.s: 奶奶常说：“{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，一家人在一起的日子要珍惜。”
ctx.en: Grandma always says: "You never know what tomorrow brings, so treasure the days the family is together."

ctx.s: 听说老同学的工厂一夜之间被大火烧光了，大家都感叹{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}。
ctx.en: When we heard an old classmate's factory had burned down overnight, we all sighed at how suddenly disaster can strike.

ctx.s: 正因为{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，他一直坚持在银行里留一笔应急的钱。
ctx.en: It is precisely because misfortune can come out of nowhere that he always keeps some emergency money in the bank.

bad.s: 明天可能会下雨，{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}，记得带伞。
bad.en: (meant: it may rain tomorrow, so remember your umbrella)
bad.why: Despite the wind and clouds, it is not about the weather: it is about sudden misfortune in people's lives.

bad.s: 他考试前一点儿也没复习，结果没及格，真是{天有不测风云，人有旦夕祸福}。
bad.en: (meant: he didn't study at all and failed)
bad.why: Failing after not studying was entirely foreseeable; the saying is only for blows that nobody could have predicted.

cards.r: fēng shuǐ lún liú zhuàn
cards.mean: fortunes rise and fall; everyone gets a turn at the top
cards.lit: good feng shui turns round from one house to the next

use.how: Said as a comment when the one who used to be on top falls and another rises, often with a grin by the new winner or as a warning: 别太得意，风水轮流转。

near.diff: 长江后浪推前浪 is a new generation overtaking the old for good; 风水轮流转 is luck changing hands, so the one now down may rise again.

cards.cue: For years your team came last in the office quiz while another team always won. This year you win and they come last. What do you say, grinning?

ctx.s: 去年他们赢了我们，今年我们赢回来了，{风水轮流转}嘛。
ctx.en: They beat us last year and this year we beat them back. Everyone gets their turn.

ctx.s: 以前总是我求他帮忙，现在轮到他来求我了，真是{风水轮流转}。
ctx.en: I used to be the one asking him for favours, and now he's asking me. The tables really have turned.

ctx.s: 别太得意，{风水轮流转}，说不定明年就轮到别人了。
ctx.en: Don't get too cocky. Luck moves on, and next year it may be someone else's turn.

ctx.s: 这家小店从前没什么人去，现在门口天天排队，老板笑着说：“{风水轮流转}啊！”
ctx.en: Hardly anyone used to go to this little shop; now there's a queue every day. The owner laughs: "It's our turn now!"

ctx.s: 几年前这个行业最赚钱，现在却不景气，{风水轮流转}，谁也说不准。
ctx.en: A few years ago this was the most profitable industry; now it's in a slump. Fortunes come and go, and nobody can say what's next.

ctx.s: 打牌连输了十几把，他终于赢了一把，高兴地喊道：“{风水轮流转}，总算到我了！”
ctx.en: After losing more than ten hands in a row he finally won one and shouted: "Luck comes round, and at last it's my turn!"

bad.s: 我们家每年都{风水轮流转}，把家具的位置换一换。
bad.en: (meant: every year our family rearranges the furniture for good feng shui)
bad.why: It is not about arranging a home by feng shui; it says fortune passes from one person or group to another.

bad.s: 他从小到大一直是班里第一名，真是{风水轮流转}。
bad.en: (meant: he has always been top of the class)
bad.why: The saying describes the top place changing hands; someone who stays on top is the very opposite.

cards.r: bù dào huáng hé xīn bù sǐ
cards.mean: to refuse to give up until every hope is gone
cards.lit: until he reaches the Yellow River, his heart won't die

use.how: Describes a stubborn person who keeps on with a hopeless plan until they hit the dead end themselves; often 他这个人不到黄河心不死。 Usually exasperated, not admiring.

near.diff: 不见棺材不落泪 is refusing to admit fault or defeat until faced with hard proof; 不到黄河心不死 is refusing to drop a hope or plan.
死马当活马医 is trying a last remedy while knowing it is hopeless; 不到黄河心不死 is refusing to accept it is hopeless at all.

cards.cue: Every publisher has turned down your friend's novel and everyone tells him to stop, but he insists on sending it to the last two anyway. How do you describe him, with a sigh?

ctx.s: 他这个人{不到黄河心不死}，劝也没用。
ctx.en: He's the type who won't give up till he hits a brick wall. There's no point trying to talk him out of it.

ctx.s: 都被拒绝三次了，你还要去？真是{不到黄河心不死}。
ctx.en: You've been turned down three times and you're still going? You just won't give up until there's no hope left.

ctx.s: 妈妈叹气说：“这孩子{不到黄河心不死}，让他自己去碰碰钉子吧。”
ctx.en: Mum sighed: "This child won't listen until he's run into the wall himself. Let him find out the hard way."

ctx.s: 明知道这个项目没希望了，老板还是{不到黄河心不死}，又投了一笔钱。
ctx.en: Everyone knew the project was hopeless, but the boss refused to give up and put in more money.

ctx.s: 已经连着落榜两次了，他还是{不到黄河心不死}，今年又报了名。
ctx.en: He has already failed the entrance exam twice, but he still won't give up: he has signed up again this year.

ctx.s: 有些人{不到黄河心不死}，非得亲身吃了亏才会回头。
ctx.en: Some people won't give up until all hope is gone; they only turn back after they've been burned themselves.

bad.s: 他学习{不到黄河心不死}，每天都努力到深夜，真让人佩服。
bad.en: (meant: he is admirably persistent in his studies)
bad.why: It mocks stubbornness in a lost cause; it is not praise for hard work or perseverance.

bad.s: 他遇到一点儿困难就放弃了，真是{不到黄河心不死}。
bad.en: (meant: he gives up at the first difficulty)
bad.why: It describes someone who refuses to give up even when it is hopeless, the opposite of quitting easily.

cards.r: hǎo mǎ bù chī huí tóu cǎo
cards.mean: a person with pride doesn't go back to what they have left
cards.lit: a good horse doesn't turn back to eat the grass it has passed

use.how: Said about returning to a former partner, employer or place one chose to leave, as a reason not to go back: 我不会回去的，好马不吃回头草。

near.diff: 天涯何处无芳草 comforts someone after a breakup that others are out there; 好马不吃回头草 says going back would be beneath you.

cards.cue: Six months after you quit, your old boss phones and offers you your job back at the same pay. You turn it down with your pride intact. What do you say?

ctx.s: 我已经辞职了，{好马不吃回头草}，不会再回去。
ctx.en: I've already resigned. I don't go back to what I've left, so I won't return.

ctx.s: 前男友想跟她复合，她只回了一句：“{好马不吃回头草}。”
ctx.en: Her ex wanted to get back together, and she replied with a single line: "I don't go backwards."

ctx.s: 分手以后，朋友们都劝她{好马不吃回头草}，别再联系那个人了。
ctx.en: After the breakup her friends all told her not to go back to him and to stop contacting him.

ctx.s: 老公司请他回去当经理，他有点犹豫：{好马不吃回头草}，可条件确实不错。
ctx.en: His old company asked him back as a manager. He hesitated: a proud man doesn't go back, but the offer really was good.

ctx.s: 谁说{好马不吃回头草}？只要那份工作适合你，回去又怎么样？
ctx.en: Who says you can never go back? If the job suits you, what's wrong with returning?

ctx.s: 当年他一气之下离开了家乡的工厂，因为{好马不吃回头草}，再苦也没回去过。
ctx.en: Years ago he walked out of his hometown factory in anger, and out of pride he never went back, however hard things got.

bad.s: 这家饭馆很好吃，可我{好马不吃回头草}，下次想换一家试试。
bad.en: (meant: I like to try a new restaurant each time)
bad.why: It is about the pride of not returning to a person or job you left, not about liking variety.

bad.s: 他犯了大错，被公司开除了，真是{好马不吃回头草}。
bad.en: (meant: he made a big mistake and was fired)
bad.why: It describes someone's own proud choice not to go back, not being thrown out by others.

cards.r: shā jī gěi hóu kàn
cards.mean: to punish one person as a warning to all the others
cards.lit: to kill a chicken for the monkeys to watch

use.how: Said about someone in authority who makes an example of one person; often used to see through the motive: 这是杀鸡给猴看。

near.diff: 枪打出头鸟 says whoever stands out gets attacked first; 杀鸡给猴看 is about the punisher's aim of frightening everyone else.

cards.cue: Thirty students copied the same homework, but the teacher punished only one of them, loudly and in front of the whole class, so the rest would get the message. What was the teacher doing?

ctx.s: 老师当着全班的面批评他，其实是{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: The teacher criticised him in front of the whole class, but really it was a warning to everyone else.

ctx.s: 公司开除了一个经常迟到的员工，大家都明白这是{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: The company fired one employee who was often late, and everyone understood it was meant as a warning to the rest of us.

ctx.s: 为什么只罚我一个人？不就是想{杀鸡给猴看}吗？
ctx.en: Why punish only me? Isn't it just to make an example of me?

ctx.s: 好几个人一起作弊，校长却只处分了班长，大家私下说这是{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: Several students cheated together, but the head only disciplined the class monitor. Privately everyone said he was making an example of him.

ctx.s: 教练让迟到的主力坐了一整场替补席，就是要{杀鸡给猴看}。
ctx.en: The coach kept the star player who'd turned up late on the bench for the whole match, precisely to send a message to the others.

ctx.s: 市场管理部门重罚了一家卖假货的商店，{杀鸡给猴看}，其他商家马上老实了。
ctx.en: The market regulators fined one shop selling fakes heavily as an example, and the other sellers fell into line at once.

bad.s: 老板奖励了最努力的员工，这是{杀鸡给猴看}，鼓励大家向他学习。
bad.en: (meant: the boss rewarded the hardest worker to encourage everyone)
bad.why: It is about punishing one person to frighten others, never about rewarding someone as a good example.

bad.s: 老师把全班同学都罚站了，真是{杀鸡给猴看}。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher punished the whole class)
bad.why: The point is punishing just one so the others take warning; punishing everybody is not making an example.

cards.r: yú yǔ xióng zhǎng bù kě jiān dé
cards.mean: you can't have both of two good things; you must choose
cards.lit: fish and bear's paw cannot both be had

story.text: Mencius said: fish is something I want, and bear's paw, a great delicacy, is also something I want; if I cannot have both, I will give up the fish and take the bear's paw. In the same way, life is something I want and righteousness is also something I want; if I cannot have both, I will give up life and choose righteousness.

use.how: Said as a comment when someone wants two attractive things that exclude each other; also 鱼和熊掌不可兼得. Often followed by advice to choose: 你得自己选。

near.diff: 两全其美 describes a solution that satisfies both sides at once; 鱼与熊掌不可兼得 says no such solution exists here.

cards.cue: Your friend has two offers: a well-paid job in a distant city, or a modest one near her family. She keeps hoping to have both. What do you tell her?

ctx.s: 又想要高工资又想要轻松，{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}啊。
ctx.en: You want a high salary and an easy job too? You can't have it both ways.

ctx.s: 大城市机会多，小城市生活舒服，{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}，你得自己选。
ctx.en: A big city has more opportunities and a small town is more comfortable. You can't have both, so you'll have to choose.

ctx.s: “我既想出国读书，又不想离开家人。”“{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}，总要放弃一个。”
ctx.en: "I want to study abroad, but I don't want to leave my family." "You can't have both; you'll have to give one up."

ctx.s: 这款手机拍照很好，电池却不耐用，看来{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
ctx.en: This phone takes great photos but the battery doesn't last. It seems you can't have both.

ctx.s: 她最后选择留在家里照顾孩子，暂时放下了事业，毕竟{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
ctx.en: In the end she chose to stay home with the children and put her career on hold. After all, you can't have everything.

ctx.s: 在自由和稳定之间，很多年轻人觉得{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
ctx.en: Between freedom and security, many young people feel they can't have both.

bad.s: 他既有钱又有时间，真是{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
bad.en: (meant: he is lucky enough to have both money and time)
bad.why: The saying denies that you can have both; it cannot describe someone who actually has both.

bad.s: 他又懒又粗心，真是{鱼与熊掌不可兼得}。
bad.en: (meant: he has two faults at once)
bad.why: It is about having to choose between two good things, not about someone having two bad qualities.

cards.r: péi le fū rén yòu zhé bīng
cards.mean: to lose twice over when one's own scheme backfires
cards.lit: to lose the lady and lose the soldiers as well

story.text: Zhou Yu of Wu planned to lure Liu Bei to Wu with a false offer of marriage to Sun Quan's sister and hold him until Jingzhou was handed over. Zhuge Liang saw through it; the bride's mother, the dowager of Wu, took a liking to Liu Bei, and the marriage became real. Liu Bei then slipped away with his bride, Zhou Yu's pursuing troops were beaten, and Zhuge Liang's soldiers jeered: Zhou Yu's brilliant plan to secure the realm has lost him the lady and his soldiers too.

use.how: Used as a predicate or after 真是 / 落得个 about someone whose scheme to gain something ends in a double loss; often mocking: 结果赔了夫人又折兵。

near.diff: Both are about a scheme backfiring; 偷鸡不成蚀把米 is a small loss from a petty trick, 赔了夫人又折兵 a heavier double loss, often from a clever plan.
竹篮打水一场空 is effort that yields nothing; 赔了夫人又折兵 is a scheme that leaves you worse off than before, twice over.

cards.cue: To win a contract, a company slashed its prices far below cost. It still lost the contract, and the price war left it with huge losses. How do people mock the result?

ctx.s: 他本想借合作把对手挤走，结果客户丢了，合伙人也走了，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: He planned to use the partnership to squeeze out his rival; instead he lost his clients and his partner walked out too. A double loss.

ctx.s: 为了省钱买了便宜货，没用几天就坏了，修又花了一大笔，真是{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: I bought the cheap one to save money; it broke within days and the repair cost a fortune. I lost twice over.

ctx.s: “你不是托人走后门了吗？”“别提了，礼也送了，事也没办成，{赔了夫人又折兵}。”
ctx.en: "Didn't you pull some strings?" "Don't ask. I gave the gifts and still got nothing done. Lost on both ends."

ctx.s: 那家公司想靠降价挤走对手，结果对手没走，自己倒亏了一大笔，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: The company tried to drive its rival out with price cuts, but the rival stayed and it lost a fortune instead: a scheme that backfired twice.

ctx.s: 他装病想逃掉考试，被老师发现后不但要补考，还挨了处分，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: He faked illness to get out of the exam; when the teacher found out, he had to resit it and was disciplined as well. A double loss.

ctx.s: 有人借钱炒股想赚快钱，最后本钱利息全赔进去，落得个{赔了夫人又折兵}。
ctx.en: Some people borrow money to play the stock market for quick gains, and end up losing both the capital and the interest: their scheme costs them twice.

bad.s: 他出了车祸，人受了伤，车也撞坏了，真是{赔了夫人又折兵}。
bad.en: (meant: he was injured and his car was wrecked in an accident)
bad.why: An accident is bad luck, not one's own scheme backfiring; the saying always blames a plan that went wrong.

bad.s: 他去年离了婚，今年又丢了工作，{赔了夫人又折兵}。
bad.en: (meant: he lost his wife and then his job)
bad.why: The lady comes from the story; the saying is about a scheme that backfires, not literally losing a wife.

cards.r: zhú lán dǎ shuǐ yī chǎng kōng
cards.mean: all one's efforts come to nothing in the end
cards.lit: drawing water with a bamboo basket: all for nothing

use.how: Describes effort, time or hope that ended with nothing to show for it; often after 结果, 到头来 or 最后: 忙了半天，到头来竹篮打水一场空。

near.diff: 赔了夫人又折兵 is a scheme that backfires and costs you twice; 竹篮打水一场空 is simply effort that yields nothing.

cards.cue: A student prepared for months for a scholarship exam, only to find out on the day that her application had never been registered. How does she describe all that work?

ctx.s: 忙了一整年，最后{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: A whole year of hard work, and in the end it all came to nothing.

ctx.s: 如果方法不对，再努力也是{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: If your method is wrong, however hard you try, it's all wasted effort.

ctx.s: “你追了她三年，结果呢？”“别提了，{竹篮打水一场空}。”
ctx.en: "You chased her for three years. So what happened?" "Don't ask. All for nothing."

ctx.s: 他辛辛苦苦存了好几年的钱，一下子全被骗走了，到头来{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: He'd scrimped and saved for years, and then lost it all at once to a scam. All those years came to nothing.

ctx.s: 文件没保存，电脑突然死机了，几天的工夫{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: I hadn't saved the file and the computer suddenly crashed. Days of work, gone for nothing.

ctx.s: 球队拼了整整九十分钟，却在最后一刻被对手进球，所有努力{竹篮打水一场空}。
ctx.en: The team fought for the full ninety minutes, only to concede in the last moment. All that effort came to nothing.

bad.s: 孩子们都搬走了，家里{竹篮打水一场空}。
bad.en: (meant: the children have moved out and the house feels empty)
bad.why: The emptiness is of wasted effort, not of an empty house or loneliness.

bad.s: 这次考试我根本没复习，所以{竹篮打水一场空}。
bad.en: (meant: I didn't study at all, so I failed)
bad.why: It needs real effort that was wasted; with no effort put in, there was nothing to come to nothing.

cards.r: rén bǐ rén, qì sǐ rén
cards.mean: comparing yourself with others only makes you miserable
cards.lit: comparing person with person makes a person furious

use.how: Said as a whole sentence, ruefully or jokingly, after comparing oneself with someone luckier, or to tell someone to stop comparing: 别比了，人比人，气死人。

near.diff: 山外有山，人外有人 is a call to stay modest because someone is always better; 人比人，气死人 is about the misery comparison brings.

cards.cue: Your old roommate has just posted photos of her new house and her promotion, while you are still renting a shared flat. You put down your phone and sigh.

ctx.s: 别老跟别人比了，{人比人，气死人}。
ctx.en: Stop comparing yourself with other people all the time. It'll only make you miserable.

ctx.s: 同样是毕业五年，他已经买了房，我还在租房，真是{人比人，气死人}。
ctx.en: We both graduated five years ago; he's bought a flat and I'm still renting. Comparing just drives you mad.

ctx.s: “你看人家孩子，又考了第一。”“妈，{人比人，气死人}，您就别比了。”
ctx.en: "Look at their kid, top of the class again." "Mum, comparing only upsets everyone. Please stop."

ctx.s: 哥哥吃多少都不胖，我喝口水都长肉，{人比人，气死人}啊！
ctx.en: My brother can eat anything and never gains weight, while I put on pounds just drinking water. Life's so unfair when you compare!

ctx.s: 朋友圈里人人都在旅游，她看了一会儿就关了手机，心想：{人比人，气死人}。
ctx.en: Everyone on her social feed seemed to be on holiday. After a while she switched off her phone, thinking: comparing only makes you miserable.

ctx.s: 幸福是自己的感觉，{人比人，气死人}，过好自己的日子就行了。
ctx.en: Happiness is about how you feel yourself. Comparing only brings misery, so just live your own life well.

bad.s: 他们俩在操场上比赛谁跑得快，{人比人，气死人}。
bad.en: (meant: the two of them raced each other on the sports field)
bad.why: It is not about a contest between people; it is about feeling bad when you measure your own lot against someone else's.

bad.s: 他说话太难听了，{人比人，气死人}。
bad.en: (meant: what he said was so rude it made me furious)
bad.why: The anger comes from comparing yourself with others, not from someone's rude words.

cards.r: yǎn bù jiàn, xīn bù fán
cards.mean: what you don't see can't upset you
cards.lit: if the eyes don't see it, the heart isn't annoyed

use.how: Said as a reason for deliberately not looking at something irritating you cannot change: shutting a door, leaving, deleting a contact: 我干脆不看了，眼不见，心不烦。

near.diff: 眼不见为净 is often about ignoring something dirty or unpleasant you'd rather not know about; 眼不见，心不烦 is about avoiding irritation.

cards.cue: Your teenage son's bedroom is a disaster and nagging hasn't helped, so you simply keep his door closed and stop going in. Why?

ctx.s: 他的房间太乱了，我干脆把门关上，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: His room is such a mess that I just shut the door. What I don't see can't annoy me.

ctx.s: “你怎么把他的微信删了？”“{眼不见，心不烦}嘛。”
ctx.en: "Why did you delete him from WeChat?" "If I can't see his posts, they can't annoy me."

ctx.s: 孩子打游戏我也管不了，就出门散步去了，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: I can't stop the kids gaming anyway, so I went out for a walk. What I don't see can't bother me.

ctx.s: 股票跌得厉害，他索性把软件卸载了，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: His shares were plunging, so he simply deleted the app. If he couldn't see it, it couldn't upset him.

ctx.s: 搬出合租房以后，再也不用看室友把脏碗堆在水池里，真是{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: Since I moved out of the shared flat, I no longer have to watch my flatmate pile dirty dishes in the sink. What a relief not to see it.

ctx.s: 她知道丈夫抽烟改不了，只要求他去阳台抽，{眼不见，心不烦}。
ctx.en: She knew her husband would never quit smoking, so she just asked him to do it on the balcony, where she wouldn't have to see it.

bad.s: 我眼睛不好，看不清黑板，{眼不见，心不烦}。
bad.en: (meant: my eyesight is poor and I can't see the board, which worries me)
bad.why: It is not about poor eyesight; it means choosing not to look at something so that it stops annoying you.

bad.s: 他一天没见到女朋友就特别想她，真是{眼不见，心不烦}。
bad.en: (meant: when he doesn't see his girlfriend he misses her)
bad.why: It says not seeing something stops it bothering you; missing someone you can't see is the opposite feeling.
